benefit_desc: There are several situations in which a company must proactively delete personal information: when a service is discontinued, when the agreed retention period ends, when you withdraw consent, or when the original purpose of data collection has been fulfilled. If it fails to do so, you can demand deletion. Should it deny your rights without justification, you may file a lawsuit.
plain_terms: You have the right to demand that a company let you view, copy, correct, and delete your personal information. When a service is discontinued, its retention period expires, or you withdraw consent, the company is obligated to delete that data on its own. If it refuses your request, it must provide a valid reason; otherwise, you can take it to court. Deactivating an account and deleting personal information are two separate actions — after deactivating, you must separately request deletion.
notes: Deactivating an account and deleting personal information are distinct processes; after deactivating, you must separately request deletion. Before switching phones or selling an old device, make sure to log out of all accounts, unlink them, and then perform a factory reset. The law grants you a right to deletion after the fact — it cannot retrieve data that has already been leaked.

title: You’re not required to use facial recognition: if other options exist, they must offer you alternatives if you refuse
cost_desc: No cost involved. When asked to use facial recognition, simply ask, “Are there any other verification methods available?” If they claim none exist, demand they provide alternatives. The challenge lies in actually voicing this question on the spot.
benefit_desc: The Administrative Measures for the Safe Use of Facial Recognition Technology clearly state: “Where other non-facial recognition technologies can achieve the same purpose or meet equivalent operational requirements, facial recognition must not be used as the sole verification method. If an individual declines facial recognition for identity verification, other reasonable and convenient alternatives must be provided.” The measures further stipulate: “No organization or individual may mislead, deceive, or coerce individuals into accepting facial recognition for identity verification under the pretext of service delivery or improved quality.” Consent to use facial recognition must be “freely, explicitly, and separately given after full disclosure” — meaning you must be asked specifically about this and must agree independently. You retain the right to withdraw consent, and service providers must offer an easy way to do so. For minors under 14, parental or guardian consent is mandatory. In public spaces, facial recognition devices may only be installed if “necessary for public safety” and must display prominent warning signs. Their use inside private areas such as hotel rooms, showers, changing rooms, or restrooms is forbidden. Facial data must be stored locally on devices and must not be transmitted over the internet, except where permitted by law or with explicit consent (effective nationwide as of June 1, 2025).
plain_terms: As long as any other method can achieve the same result, a service provider cannot force you to use facial recognition. If you decline facial recognition, they must offer alternatives such as a card swipe, password entry, or ID verification. They also cannot threaten that “the service won’t be provided” if you refuse. Installing facial recognition devices in hotel rooms, public showers, changing rooms, or restrooms is strictly prohibited.
notes: Common scenarios include residential building access systems, rental platforms, gyms, and hotels requesting facial data. When they claim “the system only supports facial recognition,” quote the exact wording from the regulations: “Where other non-facial recognition technologies can achieve the same purpose or meet equivalent operational requirements, facial recognition must not be used as the sole verification method.” Then demand alternative verification methods such as card swipes, passwords, or ID checks. If they still refuse, report them to local internet regulatory authorities. Certain financial and government services may have separate rules — follow those instead. Unlike passwords, facial data cannot be changed after a breach, so it demands greater caution. Organizations storing facial data on behalf of 100,000+ individuals must register with provincial or higher-level internet regulators within 30 days; this registration status can help you assess their legitimacy. Your rights to access, correct, or delete your personal data are covered in item 8.

title: Do not entrust proprietary code, API keys, or confidential data to unverified "AI relay proxy stations," especially when allowing AI agents to execute local commands autonomously
cost_desc: Direct official API access is typically more expensive than third-party relay proxies, and recharging balances can be less convenient. The friction lies in the temptation: relay proxies are cheap and provide access to multiple foundational models through a single endpoint.
benefit_desc: In June 2026, the Ministry of State Security issued a cybersecurity advisory warning that unverified third-party proxy relays retain submitted user data on remote servers, intercept proprietary code, or resell private datasets to other model providers for training. Some proxies conceal backdoors, injecting malicious payloads into user devices to harvest credentials and install remote administration trojans. The advisory strongly recommends using direct official API connections or officially licensed platforms while avoiding unlicensed, unverified proxies. Sensitive data and project documentation should be sanitized and desensitized before transmission, and API keys must be rotated regularly. If abnormal billing, unexplained bans, or data anomalies occur, discontinue service immediately, revoke keys, scan for malware, and preserve evidence. A 2026 empirical study by researchers at UC Santa Barbara and collaborator institutions evaluated 28 commercial relay services purchased across online storefronts and 400 public free proxies. Results showed that 1 paid service and 8 free proxies injected malicious code into returned tool-call outputs (system commands instructed by the AI to run on local machines, such as package installations). Furthermore, 2 services strategically timed their attacks, selectively targeting fully autonomous agent execution sessions. Seventeen proxies actively abused intentionally placed Amazon Web Services (AWS) credentials, and 1 drained test funds from an Ethereum test wallet (loss under $50). The study demonstrated subtle, stealthy tampering techniques: for instance, replacing standard packages like `requests` with typosquatted dependencies like `reqeusts` in command payloads, which easily escapes visual inspection.
plain_terms: An intermediary proxy sits directly between you and the model provider: it can observe, intercept, and modify everything you send and receive. In an empirical study evaluating over 400 proxy stations, 9 injected malicious code into model responses, and 17 actively hijacked intentionally seeded cloud service credentials. If you allow AI agents to execute commands locally on your machine, a single tampered command is enough to compromise full system control.
notes: Rated Grade B because it relies on a single empirical preprint prior to peer-reviewed publication. The majority of evaluated relays were free public endpoints, with only 28 commercial services tested, precluding an exact statistical percentage of compromised market share. Some media reports mistakenly exaggerated the test wallet theft to $500,000; the actual loss reported in the paper was under $50. Benefit is rated medium due to the severity of credential leaks and device takeover risks, though individual financial losses vary. If you have previously routed sensitive requests through unknown proxies, immediately revoke and regenerate affected API keys with the official model provider, as well as any exposed cloud provider and code repository access tokens. When routing through third-party proxies, never grant AI agents unreviewed autonomous command execution—manually inspect every shell command before confirmation. For criminal liabilities associated with operating unauthorized proxy relays, see Chapter 11, Rule 19.

title: Audit SIM cards and bank cards registered under your national identity once a year, and cancel unauthorized cards immediately
cost_desc: Zero financial cost. Check SIM cards via the "MIIT Micro-Report" official WeChat account or the "One ID All Queries" mini-program on Alipay. Audit bank cards via the "One-Click Card Query" feature within the China UnionPay (UnionPay QuickPass) app. Each query takes only a few minutes, with results dispatched via SMS within 1 to 2 days. The difficulty is self-discipline—remembering an unprompted annual security audit.
benefit_desc: The Anti-Telecom and Online Fraud Law mandates that telecommunications authorities provide convenient channels for citizens to query SIM cards registered under their identities, and the People's Bank of China must ensure convenient verification tools for bank accounts and payment accounts. The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) launched the national "One ID All Queries" mobile card verification portal on September 14, 2021. Entering your citizen ID number returns total registered SIM card counts across all three major telecom operators. The service was deployed because nationwide anti-fraud crackdowns revealed that vast numbers of fraud SIMs were registered under innocent citizens whose identities had been misappropriated, inflicting reputational and credit harm. Verification results arrive within 48 hours via SMS from 10699000; discrepancies can be audited at operator service centers to verify, unbundle, freeze, or terminate fraudulent lines. In July 2022, MIIT introduced "One ID All Queries 2.0," which queries the total number of major internet platform accounts (including WeChat, Alipay, Baidu, Kuaishou, Douyin, JD, Meituan) bound to a phone number. For bank accounts, China UnionPay expanded "One-Click Card Query" nationwide across all provinces on June 29, 2022. Users select banks, complete biometric authentication, and receive a comprehensive, desensitized account report within 24 hours (data is automatically purged after 7 days).
plain_terms: Criminal fraudsters frequently use stolen or forged ID information to open fraudulent SIM cards and bank accounts, often leaving victims completely unaware until police freeze their accounts or credit scores drop. Free official portals allow you to query how many SIM cards are registered to your ID card, which platforms link to your phone number, and all UnionPay debit and credit cards opened in your name. If you discover unrecognized accounts, contact the telecom carrier or bank immediately to investigate and cancel them.
notes: "One-Click Card Query" is limited to UnionPay cards. Cards without a registered mobile number or with expired identity filings may not appear in the automated query; individual bank records remain definitive. Checking credit reports for unauthorized loans and credit card lines is detailed in Chapter 8, Rule 9. For phone numbers showing extensive platform bindings, unlink them before canceling the phone number (see Chapter 14, Rule 12). Lending or selling your own SIM and bank cards constitutes a criminal offense (see Chapter 8, Rule 8). Evidence Grade C reflects reliance on official government regulatory service bulletins rather than controlled trials quantifying saved financial loss. Benefit magnitude is categorized as Moderate. Beneficiary is yourself.

title: Before canceling or changing a mobile phone number, migrate or unbind all linked online services and update your bank registration
cost_desc: Zero financial outlay. Requires migrating accounts individually to your new number, and updating bank-registered mobile numbers via banking apps or physical branches. Accounts with extensive bindings take 1 to 2 hours. The difficulty is remembering rarely used legacy services.
benefit_desc: National Telecommunications Service Specifications mandate that the minimum quarantine freeze period for mobile phone numbers is 90 days (measured from cancellation to reissue), after which numbers may be reassigned to the public pool. MIIT's Q1 2025 Telecommunications Service Quality Bulletin highlighted the carrier "Recycled Number Renewal" feature within operator apps, enabling new subscribers to unbind accounts registered by previous owners prior to line activation. The Q2 2026 bulletin noted that this service covered 258 mainstream internet applications with over 850 million unbinding requests processed. The necessity of new subscribers having to unbind past accounts confirms that legacy accounts frequently remain bound to recycled numbers. In 2024 interviews with People's Posts and Telecom, carrier customer service representatives confirmed that new number owners can log into legacy accounts via SMS verification codes if previous holders failed to unbind them, strongly advising subscribers to unlink WeChat, Alipay, and bank registration numbers prior to number cancellation.
plain_terms: Once a mobile phone number is cancelled, telecommunications carriers are legally permitted to reissue that recycled number to a new subscriber after just 90 days. If your old accounts remain linked to that number, SMS two-factor verification codes will route directly to the new subscriber's handset, potentially allowing them to log into your accounts. Always migrate critical payment apps, digital wallets, and bank records before disconnecting your number.
notes: First use "One ID All Queries 2.0" to audit how many platforms are tied to your old number (see Chapter 14, Rule 11). Update high-risk financial and payment accounts first, then social platforms, and delete unused legacy accounts. After migrating accounts, maintain the old number on a minimal maintenance plan for 1 to 2 months to catch any overlooked SMS verification prompts. Managing unauthorized device logins is covered in Chapter 14, Rule 6. Sanitizing old phones and performing factory resets prior to sale is addressed in Chapter 14, Rule 8 notes. Graded Evidence Grade C due to qualitative operational advisories from carriers and regulators. Benefit is categorized as Moderate. Beneficiary is yourself.

title: The amount of the deposit, its refund timeline, and permissible deduction scenarios must be specified in the contract
cost_desc: No monetary cost. It only requires an extra ten minutes when signing the contract. The challenge lies in bringing this up in front of the landlord.
benefit_desc: Regulatory statutes make this clear: “Landlords collecting a deposit must specify the deposit amount, refund timing, and permissible deduction scenarios in the housing lease agreement. Apart from these agreed terms, landlords have no right to deduct funds without valid justification.” In short, three key points must appear in the contract: how much the deposit is, when it’s returned, and under what conditions it can be deducted. Reasons not listed in the contract cannot be used to justify any deductions.
plain_terms: The deposit amount, when it will be returned, and under what circumstances deductions are allowed must all be written into the contract before you sign it. Any deduction reasons not explicitly stated in the contract cannot be used by the landlord to withhold your deposit at the end of the lease.
notes: On the day of moving out, take photos and videos together with the landlord. Capture readings from water, electricity, and gas meters, as well as images of walls and floors. If your deposit is deducted without cause, first file a complaint with the housing regulatory authority. For smaller amounts, consider pursuing a small claims lawsuit — see Section 8 for details.

title: When water and electricity are cut off, locks are changed, or you’re threatened to leave — call the police right away: laws forbid using these tactics to force you out
cost_desc: No cost at all. Just make a phone call to the police and they’ll be there immediately.
benefit_desc: Administrative regulations make it clear: “Landlords may not use violence, threats, or any other illegal means to compel tenants to terminate a housing lease or vacate the premises.” Eviction means being forced to move out. In such situations, call the police and preserve all evidence — do not take matters into your own hands.
plain_terms: Landlords are strictly prohibited by law from cutting off utilities, changing locks, or threatening tenants to end a lease or force them to move out. If this happens to you, call the police right away. The police report serves as proof if you later seek compensation for any losses. Do not attempt to confront the landlord on your own.
notes: Calling the police ensures you obtain an official report. This report becomes crucial evidence if you later file a claim for damages. Also be sure to notify your local housing authority.

title: Real estate agents must not collect or remit rent and security deposits; payments go straight to landlords
cost_desc: No cost at all. It takes just a few minutes to verify the recipient before paying. The hard part is resisting pressure from agents who try to get you to send the money to them instead.
benefit_desc: Administrative rules explicitly forbid real estate agencies from collecting or remitting rent and security deposits on behalf of landlords. This means agents have no legal authority to handle such payments. Every time money moves through an agent’s hands, the risk of them running off with the money rises significantly.
plain_terms: By regulation, real estate agents are prohibited from collecting or remitting rent and security deposits; all payments must go directly to landlords. Any time money passes through an agent’s hands, it creates one extra chance for them to abscond with the funds. If that happens, you lose both your rent payments and your right to stay in the property. Always confirm that the recipient’s name matches the name on the property title before paying.
notes: Double-check that the recipient’s name matches the name on the property title before making any payment. If it does not, ask for a written authorization first. Agents are only allowed to charge a commission fee for their matchmaking services.

title: Check a long-term rental’s escrow account before paying a full year’s rent upfront
cost_desc: No cost at all. It takes just a few minutes to verify.
benefit_desc: Regulations require any housing rental business that sublets units to set up a dedicated escrow account for rental funds and make it visible to the public. Subletting means a company leases entire properties from landlords and then rents them out to individual tenants. The tiny discount from paying a full year’s rent upfront is far outweighed by the risk of losing both your deposit and all prepaid rent if the company shuts down. This risk is even greater if you’ve taken out a rent loan.
plain_terms: The discount you get from paying a full year’s rent upfront is minimal. If the rental company goes out of business, you lose both your security deposit and the rent you’ve prepaid for the remaining months. It gets even worse if you take out a rent loan: even if the company disappears, you’re still obligated to make all monthly loan payments. Always check whether the company has a publicly listed escrow account before signing any lease.
notes: Carefully check whether any loan products are tied to your lease agreement. If a third-party app lets you pay a full year’s rent upfront to the rental company, and you then repay that amount via monthly installments, you’ll still be responsible for all payments even if the company ceases operations. Avoid signing any such contracts.

title: House sold during lease term – lease remains valid, no need to move
cost_desc: No cost at all
benefit_desc: The Civil Code includes a principle known as “sale does not break lease,” meaning a property sale has no effect on an existing lease agreement. The actual wording is: “Any change in ownership of leased property during the lease term does not affect the validity of the lease contract.” In other words, even if the house changes hands while you’re renting it, the new owner must abide by the original terms and let you stay until the lease ends.
plain_terms: If a house is sold while you’re still renting it, your lease stays valid. The new owner must honor the original contract and let you live there until it ends. You won’t need to move out or renegotiate any terms. This only applies if you’re already living there legally; be sure to keep proof such as the lease, payment records, and documentation showing when you moved in.
notes: This applies only if you’re already residing there lawfully; the law refers to such occupancy as “legal possession and use.” It’s essential to retain all relevant documentation, including the lease, proof of payments, and records indicating your move-in date.

title: Checking property rights and mortgages before signing the contract; all payments must be transferred with a purpose note
cost_desc: No cost involved. The check takes about half an hour.
benefit_desc: These two scenarios represent the typical ways people lose all their money: paying rent to a non-owner, or dealing with a property that’s already mortgaged and seized. Keeping a transfer note that reads “Monthly rent for [property address]” provides solid evidence if a dispute arises later.
plain_terms: The two most common ways people end up losing all their money are: first, paying rent to someone who isn’t the property owner; second, discovering that the house was already mortgaged to a bank and later seized. Before signing, verify both the property rights and any existing mortgages at the local land registry office. All payments must be made via bank transfer, with a note stating “Monthly rent for [property address]”. This note serves as direct proof in case of any disputes.
notes: Property rights information can be obtained from the local land registry office. At the time of signing, the actual owner must be present; if not, a written authorization is required. If you’re renting from a sub-landlord, written consent from the original owner is mandatory.

title: For second-hand home sales where the agent collects the payment, the funds must be deposited into a dedicated transaction account opened by the agency at a bank
cost_desc: No cost involved. The challenge is ensuring the payment goes into the designated account; this may require some discussion with the agent.
benefit_desc: Regulations are explicit: any real estate agency entrusted to collect or disburse transaction funds must use a dedicated client settlement account at a bank. This ensures the payment is held in a regulated account, not the agency’s general account or any individual agent’s personal account.
plain_terms: The purchase price can range from hundreds of thousands to millions of dollars — this is the largest single transaction amount discussed in this guide. By regulation, when an agent collects payment, it must be transferred to a dedicated account opened by the agency at a bank, not sent via WeChat to the individual agent. Additionally, when two agencies collaborate on one sale, only one commission fee may be charged; services such as loan processing or title transfer require separate contracts and clear fee agreements beforehand.
notes: Given the substantial amount involved, never send payment via WeChat to an agent. Two common scenarios involving extra charges also apply: first, when two agencies jointly handle a sale, only one commission fee is allowed; second, services like loan processing or title transfer are separate and must be contracted individually with clear fee disclosures. All payments should be transferred via bank transfer with a purpose note, as outlined in item 6 (verifying property titles and mortgage status prior to signing).

title: Don’t rent a subdivided apartment: the smallest legal rental unit is the original room as designed; kitchens, bathrooms, balconies must not be used for living.
cost_desc: There’s no direct expense. The trade-off is that with the same budget, you’ll either have to live farther away or in a smaller space.
benefit_desc: The rules are clear: the smallest legal rental unit is the original room, and it cannot be subdivided into multiple units for separate rentals. The minimum per-person living area must meet local legal standards. Kitchens, bathrooms, balconies, and basements cannot be rented out for occupancy. Landlords also cannot arbitrarily increase rents during a lease term.
plain_terms: By regulation, the minimum rental unit is the original room as built. Kitchens, bathrooms, balconies, and basement storage areas cannot be used for living. If such a unit is found to be illegal, you may be forced to move out. Additionally, during the lease term, landlords cannot unilaterally raise rents at will.
notes: When illegal room subdivisions are identified, tenants bear the cost of moving out, and often cannot recover their security deposit or prepaid rent. Safety is also a concern: makeshift walls often block emergency exits, and overcrowding in a single unit leads to shared wiring. When viewing a property, check three things: whether any walls were added later, if the room has a window, and whether the electrical meter can handle the expected number of occupants.

title: Urban residents with hukou who want to live in the countryside can only rent rural houses — they must not buy homestead land or houses on it
cost_desc: No upfront cost. The trade-off is that the house remains the landlord’s property; the maximum single lease term is 20 years, after which a new agreement must be negotiated.
benefit_desc: Official documents from the General Office of the State Council make clear: “Urban residents must not purchase homestead land, rural houses, or ‘small-property houses’ in villages.” The same documents also state that after selling or leasing their homes, farmers cannot reapply for homestead land. A 2019 joint directive from the Central Rural Work Leading Group Office and the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs reiterates this ban while outlining a legal alternative: urban residents may rent rural houses for residence or business use, provided lease terms do not exceed 20 years and are mutually agreed upon upon renewal.
plain_terms: People with urban hukou are expressly prohibited by national regulations from buying homestead land, rural houses, or “small-property houses” in villages. Even if villagers claim “a written contract suffices,” paying money does not transfer ownership of the property. To reside long-term in the countryside, one must sign a lease agreement limited to 20 years per term, with renewal possible thereafter.
notes: Homestead land is allocated solely to registered villagers for construction purposes. When renting a rural house, a written contract must specify the lease term, rent amount, permission for renovations, and how any renovation costs are handled at lease end. Leases exceeding 20 years — such as 50- or 70-year terms — are illegal; likewise, paying rent for multiple years upfront is prohibited. Additionally, it is illegal to use homestead land for building villas, large estates, or private clubs; paying villagers to “co-build” such structures also violates regulations.

title: When purchasing off-plan presale property, verify the presale permit first; deposit, down payment, and mortgage funds must be deposited exclusively into the designated escrow account specified in the contract
cost_desc: Zero financial outlay. Spend a few minutes checking the presale permit and matching the bank account details before wiring funds. The challenge is standing firm when sales agents request payment to alternative auxiliary accounts.
benefit_desc: Under the August 2026 joint directive issued by the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development (MOHURD), the Ministry of Natural Resources, and the National Financial Regulatory Administration (Jianfanggui [2026] No. 3): "All homebuyer purchasing funds, including down payments and personal residential mortgages, must be deposited in full into the dedicated capital escrow account." Escrow supervision is released only after the residential building completes statutory construction acceptance and meets full operational delivery conditions for water, electricity, gas, and heating. The sales contract must explicitly delineate buyers' rights and developer duties regarding escrow deposits. If the developer defaults or fails to deliver on time, the buyer may rescind the contract and demand a full refund alongside liquidated breach damages. Furthermore, PBOC and NFRA regulations dictate that commercial banks must disburse personal mortgage proceeds directly into the project's designated presale escrow account. Prior regulations (2010 and 2022) established that developers lacking presale permits may not collect deposits via pre-reservations, VIP memberships, or numbering queues; presale contracts signed without a valid presale permit are judged legally void by civil courts unless the permit is cured prior to litigation.
plain_terms: Off-plan presale property refers to residential real estate sold prior to construction completion. Without a valid statutory presale permit, developers are legally barred from selling units or collecting deposits. By regulation, all earnest money, down payments, and bank mortgages must flow directly into an official government-monitored presale escrow account, which cannot be released until the property passes final completion inspection and meets full utility connection standards. Routing funds to any non-escrow account forfeits statutory protection.
notes: For projects that obtained construction planning permits prior to August 28, 2026, local transitional presale supervision rules apply. For completed existing housing where earnest money is paid prior to contract execution, regulations mandate deposit into a dedicated earnest deposit escrow account. The exact account name and number must be verified directly against the standardized sales contract before transferring funds. If a contract is declared void and a developer refuses repayment, civil litigation takes 6+ months with legal fees paid by the plaintiff. Depositing secondary housing funds is covered in Chapter 15, Rule 7. Benefit magnitude is categorized as High based on preventing total loss of housing capital. Primary beneficiaries are yourself and your household.

title: If a formal contract cannot be finalized or mortgage financing is denied due to reasons not attributable to either party after paying a reservation deposit or down payment, demand a full refund
cost_desc: Zero monetary cost. Review mortgage contingency and earnest clauses carefully when executing reservation agreements and formal purchase contracts. If a developer refuses a refund, civil litigation is required.
benefit_desc: Under Supreme People's Court judicial interpretations on commodity housing contracts: where earnest money is collected through reservation or subscription agreements and the formal contract cannot be concluded due to fault of one party, standard earnest deposit rules apply (the defaulting depositor forfeits the deposit; the defaulting receiver pays double). However, if the formal sales contract cannot be concluded due to causes not attributable to either party, "the seller shall return the earnest deposit to the buyer." Regarding mortgage financing: where the purchase contract stipulates mortgage financing but the loan contract cannot be finalized, rendering contract performance impossible due to causes not attributable to either party, both parties are entitled to rescind the purchase contract. In such circumstances, the developer must fully refund all received purchase principal alongside accrued interest or refund the earnest deposit. Circumstances not attributable to either party include unexpected macroeconomic mortgage tightening or sudden regulatory credit quotas imposed post-signing. Conversely, failure caused by the buyer's credit delinquency or unverified income represents buyer fault, whereas developer project licensing deficiencies or bank blacklisting represent developer fault.
plain_terms: When you pay a reservation deposit or down payment but a formal sales contract cannot be executed, or mortgage financing fails due to non-fault causes (such as unexpected policy tightening or sudden bank lending moratoriums), the developer is legally obligated to refund your deposit or purchase funds with interest. If loan rejection results from your personal credit defaults or inadequate income documentation, the deposit is forfeited. If rejection stems from developer permitting defects, the developer must return double the earnest money.
notes: In judicial practice, determining whether financing failure was "not attributable to either party" is evaluated on a case-by-case basis. To safeguard rights, explicitly write financing contingency clauses into the purchase agreement stating what remedies apply if mortgage approval is denied. If a subscription agreement already contains all essential terms of a commodity housing sales contract and the developer has collected housing funds, courts will treat the subscription as a binding sales contract rather than an unexecuted reservation. Pursuing refunds through courts takes 3 to 6 months. Benefit magnitude is categorized as High based on recovering hundreds of thousands in deposits. Primary beneficiaries are yourself and your family.

title: Clarify floor area discrepancy remedies before signing a new home contract, and preserve photographic evidence of promotional brochures, advertisements, and architectural scale models
cost_desc: Zero financial outlay. Review the area error terms before signing and photograph marketing scale models, promotional renderings, and sales brochures.
benefit_desc: Under the Measures for the Administration of the Sale of Commodity Housing (Ministry of Construction Order No. 88), purchase contracts pricing property by floor area must specify discrepancy settlement terms. Where contracts contain no alternative provisions, statutory defaults apply: 1) For absolute area discrepancies within 3% (inclusive), payments are settled based on actual delivered area. 2) If area discrepancy exceeds 3%, the buyer has the legal right to rescind the contract. Upon rescission, the developer must refund all payments with accrued bank interest within 30 days of notice. If the buyer retains the property: when delivered area exceeds contract area by over 3%, the buyer pays for the initial 3% discrepancy, while area beyond 3% is conveyed free to the buyer with title transferred; when delivered area is less than contract area by over 3%, the developer refunds the shortfall within 3% and refunds double the shortfall exceeding 3%. Regarding advertising promises, Supreme People's Court judicial interpretations establish that while general sales advertisements constitute invitations to offer, specific and definite descriptions or commitments made by developers regarding housing specifications or community amenities within the project planning scope that have a material impact on purchase decisions are deemed binding contract terms: "Even if such representations and promises are not incorporated into the commodity housing sales contract, they shall constitute terms of the contract," and violations establish actionable breach of contract.
plain_terms: Unless the sales contract specifies otherwise, if the registered deed area of a delivered home differs from the contract area by 3% or less, payments are settled on actual area. If the discrepancy exceeds 3%, you are legally entitled to cancel the purchase, and the developer must refund your money with interest within 30 days. Furthermore, specific, concrete promotional promises regarding amenities or specifications within the project development boundary form binding contract terms, even if omitted from the final written contract.
notes: The 3% rule serves as the statutory default when the contract does not stipulate otherwise; always examine sales contract templates to ensure developers have not inserted clauses waiving this protection or expanding error tolerances. For units sold on a lump-sum whole-unit basis, contracts must attach architectural layout diagrams specifying dimensional tolerances. The advertising binding rule applies strictly to properties and facilities within the approved zoning and planning boundaries of the development project, and does not extend to external public infrastructure (schools, subway stations, public parks) outside developer property lines. Preserve all original promotional collateral, print brochures, and timestamped photos of the sales hall model. Benefit magnitude is categorized as Moderate based on financial compensation. Primary beneficiaries are yourself and your household.

title: If a developer delays property delivery or deed registration, serve a formal written notice of demand to preserve evidence, then claim contractual liquidated damages
cost_desc: Zero monetary cost. Draft a formal written demand notice, deliver it via registered certified mail with return receipt, and archive delivery tracking. Rescinding the contract or suing for damages requires formal legal proceedings.
benefit_desc: Under Supreme People's Court judicial interpretations: where a developer defaults on property delivery and fails to perform within 3 months following buyer formal demand notice, the buyer is entitled to rescind the contract, unless otherwise agreed. The right of rescission is subject to statutory forfeiture periods: if the developer serves a formal notice demanding the buyer elect remedies, the right must be exercised within 3 months; if no notice is given, it must be exercised within 1 year from the date the right accrued, after which the right is extinguished. Where the contract does not stipulate liquidated damages or loss calculation formulas, delayed delivery compensation is determined by official guidance or certified appraisals of fair market rental value for comparable housing in the same locality during the delay period. Regarding property ownership certificates: the developer is liable for breach if deed registration is uncompleted by contractual deadlines, within 90 days of delivery for off-plan presale property, or within 90 days of contract signing for existing completed property. Where the contract omits liquidated damages, compensation is calculated on total payments received based on benchmark bank overdue loan interest rates. If deed registration remains uncompleted for more than 1 year after the deadline due to developer fault, the buyer is entitled to rescind the contract and claim damages.
plain_terms: If a developer delays delivery past the contractual deadline, serve a formal written demand. If delivery remains unfulfilled 3 months after demand, you are legally entitled to rescind the purchase contract. If the contract omits liquidated damages, statutory compensation is calculated based on market rental value for comparable properties in the same neighborhood. If deed registration is delayed past statutory limits by over one year due to developer fault, you may likewise rescind and demand damages. The right of rescission has strict expiration windows, so do not remain passive.
notes: Always serve demands in writing via tracked postal delivery to the registered corporate address in the contract, archiving physical receipts and signed delivery records. When a purchase contract is rescinded, the corresponding bank mortgage contract can be rescinded concurrently: the developer must refund the mortgage loan balance directly to the bank, and refund all principal payments, down payments, and interest to the homebuyer. Liquidated damages stipulated in contracts are enforceable, though courts may adjust amounts exceeding actual losses by more than 30% upon developer petition. Ordinary civil lawsuits take 6+ months. Benefit magnitude is categorized as Moderate based on preserving legal rescission rights and recovering rental compensation. Primary beneficiaries are yourself and your family.

title: Conduct title searches for mortgages and court attachments before signing a purchase contract, and file for provisional registration immediately after signing
cost_desc: A few dozen RMB in statutory registration fees. Spend half an hour conducting an in-person title search with government ID before signing, and visit the real estate registry with the seller post-signing.
benefit_desc: Under Civil Code Article 221, parties executing a real estate transaction agreement may apply for advance notice provisional registration to secure future property rights: "After provisional registration is made, any disposition of the real property without the consent of the holder of the provisional registration shall not have effect in real rights." Provisional registration terminates if the underlying contract is rescinded or if an application for final title registration is not submitted within 90 days from the date when registration becomes possible. The Ministry of Natural Resources Implementing Rules for the Interim Regulations on Real Estate Registration apply this mechanism to both new off-plan commodity housing and secondary residential sales: during the validity of provisional registration, registries will refuse any third-party registration filings without the buyer's written consent. In off-plan presales, if a developer fails to co-apply as agreed, the buyer is legally authorized to apply unilaterally. Prior to signing, prospective buyers with transactional intent may query registry databases with their national ID to verify mortgage liens, advance registrations, objection registrations, and judicial seizures. Note that municipal online contract filing is an administrative measure and does not confer real property rights; judicial interpretations confirm that lack of administrative filing does not invalidate contracts unless explicitly made a condition precedent.
plain_terms: Before signing a home purchase agreement, visit the local real estate registry with your ID to verify whether the property has existing mortgages, court freezes, or prior registrations. Write provisional advance notice registration into the contract, and file for it immediately upon signing. Once provisional registration is recorded, the seller cannot legally sell, mortgage, or transfer the property to any third party without your written consent. You must complete final title transfer within 90 days of the property becoming eligible for full conveyance.
notes: Verifying property ownership and mortgage status prior to signing is detailed in Chapter 15, Rule 6. Because registry searches without a signed contract may not reveal the registered owner's full legal name, always cross-reference physical deed certificates with the seller's resident identity card in person. Securing provisional registration legally forecloses developer or seller secondary sales and unauthorized secondary mortgaging before deed transfer. While victims of collusive fraudulent double-selling can sue to void fraudulent contracts, litigation is costly and time-consuming; advance registration provides proactive statutory protection. Benefit magnitude is categorized as High based on securing property title. Primary beneficiaries are yourself and your household.

title: If holding a floating-rate mortgage and prevailing market rates for new mortgages drop significantly lower, negotiate a rate adjustment with your lending bank or apply for a mortgage replacement
cost_desc: Zero direct cost. Submitting an application via bank mobile apps or calling customer service takes several minutes. Banks review eligibility according to regulatory parameters.
benefit_desc: In 2024, People's Bank of China Announcement [2024] No. 11 established a dynamic interest rate pricing mechanism permitting borrowers and lending institutions to renegotiate the basis point spread over LPR for existing residential mortgages. Previously, the contracted spread remained immutable across the multi-decade loan tenure. In August 2026, the PBOC and NFRA codified this mechanism into formal financial directives (Yinfa [2026] No. 171, Art. 24): where the contracted interest rate on existing floating-rate mortgages deviates significantly from prevailing national average rates on newly issued mortgages, "borrowers may negotiate with banking financial institutions to adjust the agreed interest rate level, or apply for a newly issued floating-rate personal housing mortgage to replace existing loans, with the method chosen independently by the borrower." The replacement loan principal cannot exceed the remaining balance of the existing mortgage. Financial modeling example (equal monthly payments over 30 years on 1,000,000 RMB): at a 4.0% APR, the monthly payment is ~4,774 RMB; at 3.5% APR, monthly payment falls to ~4,490 RMB. This yields a monthly savings of ~284 RMB and cumulative interest savings of ~102,000 RMB over the 30-year loan life.
plain_terms: Floating mortgage interest rates are calculated by adding or subtracting basis points from a benchmark Loan Prime Rate (LPR). While the spread points were historically fixed for the entire loan life, financial reforms starting in 2024 permit borrowers and banks to renegotiate the spread. When your interest rate significantly exceeds the prevailing rates on newly issued mortgages, you can negotiate a downward adjustment or apply for a new floating-rate mortgage to replace the existing loan. On a 1,000,000 RMB 30-year mortgage, a 0.5% interest rate reduction saves approximately 100,000 RMB ($14,000 USD) in cumulative interest.
notes: The exact deviation threshold triggering repricing negotiations is governed by announcements issued by individual lending banks. This mechanism applies strictly to bank-issued commercial floating-rate mortgages. If a bank rejects rate adjustments and you maintain surplus liquid capital, compare investment returns against the mortgage rate to evaluate early repayment (see Chapter 5, Rule 28). Replacement loans cannot be used to cash out extra debt or exceed remaining principal balances. Benefit magnitude is categorized as High based on substantial multi-year interest savings. Primary beneficiaries are yourself and your family.

title: When taking out a mortgage on your first home, prioritize the Housing Provident Fund loan and combine it with a commercial loan only for the remainder; never take an entirely commercial mortgage
cost_desc: Zero financial fee. Involves making one or two extra trips to the municipal housing provident fund management center or designated trustee bank, and disbursement may take a few days longer than a purely commercial mortgage. Precondition: you must have continuously contributed to the provident fund for statutory minimum intervals.
benefit_desc: On May 7, 2025, the People's Bank of China (PBOC) announced lower interest rates for individual housing provident fund loans effective May 8: the rate for first-home provident fund loans with tenors over 5 years was set at 2.6% (2.1% for terms <=5 years), and second-home loans at not less than 3.075% (>5 years) and 2.525% (<=5 years). As of late 2026, this remains the effective benchmark. Commercial mortgage rates are priced off the Loan Prime Rate (LPR) plus or minus basis points; on September 20, 2026, the 5-year LPR was 3.50%, with the PBOC Q2 2026 Monetary Policy Report recording the nationwide average newly issued personal housing mortgage rate at ~3.1%. Financial simulation using equal monthly principal-and-interest installments illustrates the magnitude: on a 1,000,000 RMB 30-year loan, monthly installments at 2.6% are ~4,003 RMB vs. ~4,270 RMB at 3.1% (saving ~267 RMB monthly and ~96,000 RMB in cumulative interest over 30 years). Even with a combination loan (e.g., 600,000 RMB provident fund + 400,000 RMB commercial), monthly payments decrease by ~160 RMB, saving ~58,000 RMB in 30-year interest. For second homes, the provident fund floor (3.075%) is close to commercial rates (3.1%), yielding minimal difference.
plain_terms: The interest rate on a first-home Housing Provident Fund loan for terms over 5 years is 2.6%, compared to an average commercial mortgage rate of ~3.1% (as of mid-2026). On a 1,000,000 RMB loan over 30 years, using the provident fund saves approximately 96,000 RMB in total interest over a purely commercial loan. Because provident fund loan caps exist, borrow the maximum provident fund allocation first and cover the remaining balance with commercial lending (a combination loan).
notes: Accessing provident fund loans requires meeting four eligibility conditions: (1) contribution duration: national regulations mandate at least 6 consecutive months of full statutory contributions (contributions in other cities can be consolidated); (2) borrowing limits: maximum loan caps are determined by local municipal committees (e.g., Beijing caps single-contributor first homes at 1.2 million RMB, calculated at 200,000 RMB per year of contributions; Guangzhou caps single contributors at 1 million RMB for terms <=30 years, with building age plus loan duration <=50 years); (3) appraisal benchmarks: on existing homes, the loan limit is assessed against the lower of the contract price or government appraisal value; and (4) processing requirements: regulations mandate approval decisions within 10 days of application, followed by mortgage registration. Combined loans must satisfy both provident fund and commercial bank down payment criteria. Accumulated provident fund balances can also be withdrawn for mortgage amortization (see Chapter 5, Rule 3). Renegotiating commercial mortgage interest rate margins is covered in Chapter 15, Rule 15.

title: If a property management company cuts off water, electricity, heating, or gas to coerce payment of property fees, lodge a complaint with local housing authorities: property managers can only issue notices, sue, or arbitrate for unpaid fees
cost_desc: Zero financial outlay. Filing an administrative complaint or telephone report takes several dozen minutes. If the management company refuses to comply and you seek tort damages for incurred losses, litigation is required.
benefit_desc: Article 944 of the Civil Code establishes three clear legal principles: (1) "The property service provider shall not coerce payment of property service fees by interrupting the supply of electricity, water, heat, gas, or other utilities"; (2) Where the property service provider has rendered services pursuant to contract, owners may not refuse payment on grounds of "not accepting or having no need to accept" services; and (3) Where an owner fails to pay on time, the provider may demand payment within a reasonable cure period; if still unpaid, the provider may institute litigation or arbitration. The Regulations on Property Management mandate that owners' committees urge delinquent owners to pay, and property enterprises may file court lawsuits upon expiration. Homeowners can file administrative complaints with real estate administrative departments of local people's governments at or above the county level, which are mandated to process complaints promptly. Furthermore, Supreme People's Court judicial interpretations confirm that if a property service company unilaterally expands billing scopes, elevates fee standards, or imposes duplicate fees in violation of contracts or laws, courts must support the owner's refusal to pay such illicit fees and must support lawsuits demanding refunds of unauthorized fees already paid.
plain_terms: Property management companies are legally forbidden from cutting off electricity, water, gas, or heating to compel payment of property management fees; if encountered, complain to the local housing administrative bureau. Conversely, if the property company provides contractual services, owners cannot refuse payment on grounds that they "didn't use the service," and managers can sue for arrears. Unauthorized fee increases or duplicate charges can be lawfully withheld.
notes: The law prohibits property managers from cutting off utilities as debt-collection leverage. Delinquency in paying utility companies directly for water, power, or gas is governed differently: after notice and reasonable cure periods, statutory utility providers can suspend supply according to administrative regulations with advance warning. Regulations require utility companies to bill end users directly. If unauthorized utility cutoffs inflict direct damages (e.g. frozen pipes, ruined refrigeration, spoiled goods), recover damages via court lawsuit. First-instance ordinary procedure takes at least 6 months, and summary procedure 3 months, with unrecoverable attorney fees. Landlord lockouts or utility cutoffs in rental disputes are addressed in Chapter 15, Rule 2. Benefit is categorized as Moderate.

title: When taking delivery of a new home, inspect the property on-site and document defects in the handover record: water leaks and utility conduit defects must be repaired by the developer within statutory warranty periods
cost_desc: Zero financial cost. Spend 2 to 3 hours on handover day inspecting walls, floors, doors, windows, plumbing, and electrical outlets room by room, capturing photographs of every defect. Hiring a professional third-party inspector incurs an optional inspection fee.
benefit_desc: Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development regulations mandate that developers must provide buyers with a "Residential Quality Guarantee" and "Residential User Manual" upon delivering commercial housing. Developers bear statutory warranty repair liability commencing on the date of property delivery; the developer's warranty period to buyers cannot be shorter than the remaining balance of the construction contractor's warranty to the developer. For defects within warranty scope, developers must carry out repairs and compensate for consequential losses (excluding force majeure or homeowner misuse). Statutory minimum contractor warranties established by State Council regulations (calculated from final construction inspection acceptance) are: (1) 5 years for roof waterproofing, bathrooms with waterproofing requirements, rooms, and exterior wall leak prevention; (2) 2 heating/cooling seasons for heating and air-conditioning systems; (3) 2 years for electrical conduit wiring, water supply and drainage piping, equipment installation, and interior renovation finishes; and (4) the statutory design lifespan for foundations and core load-bearing structural elements. Supreme People's Court judicial interpretations establish: "If the seller refuses to repair or delays repairs within a reasonable timeframe, the buyer may execute repairs personally or commission third parties. The repair expenses and consequential damages incurred during the repair period shall be borne by the seller." If housing quality defects severely impair normal residential use, or if independent structural inspection confirms foundation or structural defects, buyers hold the statutory right to rescind the purchase contract and demand damages. Documenting defects on delivery day prevents developers from claiming that leaks were caused by your subsequent renovations.
plain_terms: Developers must provide a "Residential Quality Guarantee" upon handover. Statutory minimum contractor warranties require 5 years for waterproof roofs, bathrooms, and exterior walls, and 2 years for electrical wiring, plumbing, and interior finishings, running from construction acceptance. The developer's warranty to buyers cannot be shorter than the contractor's remaining warranty. If the developer delays or refuses repairs during warranty periods, you can hire third-party contractors and bill all repair costs to the developer.
notes: Specific warranty scopes and durations must be stipulated in purchase contracts; if contracts provide longer protections than statutory floors, the longer terms govern. If defects emerge, notify the developer via written registered notice and retain copies. If the developer fails to perform, file a civil claim; first-instance regular procedure takes at least 6 months with personal legal fees. Property area discrepancies are addressed in Chapter 15, Rule 12. Delays in delivery or title registration are covered in Chapter 15, Rule 13. Benefit is categorized as Moderate.

title: Take medication exactly as prescribed — don’t stop just because you feel better
cost_desc: There’s no cost at all; in fact, it saves money on future treatment for complications. Taking the pills each day takes only a few minutes. The real challenge is sticking to the regimen every single day.
benefit_desc: This finding comes from a meta-analysis that pooled data from 21 separate studies involving 46,847 participants. Compared to those who took medication irregularly, people who followed their prescription exactly had roughly 44% lower risk of dying during the same timeframe. The raw odds ratio was 0.56, with a 95% confidence interval ranging from 0.50 to 0.63; this interval represents the range within which the true value is likely to fall. When only treatments with proven effectiveness were considered, the risk reduction was about 45% (odds ratio 0.55, 95% CI 0.49–0.62).
plain_terms: People who consistently follow their doctor’s instructions when taking medication have roughly half the risk of dying during the same period compared to those who take it intermittently. This figure should be viewed with some caution. Even individuals who take fake pills consistently also have lower mortality rates, which suggests part of the benefit stems from the fact that people who stick to any medication routine tend to be more health-conscious overall. Still, the risks of skipping doses are well documented — especially for blood pressure drugs, anticoagulants, and anti-rejection medications.
notes: This is a somewhat controversial figure and one of the numbers in this guide that requires extra caution. In the same meta-analysis, individuals who consistently took placebos also showed a lower mortality rate (odds ratio 0.56, 95% CI 0.43–0.74). This indicates that a significant portion of the benefit is attributable to the “healthy adherer effect” — the tendency of people who stick to any kind of medication routine to generally maintain healthier habits. Nevertheless, the risks associated with discontinuing medication are very real, particularly for blood pressure drugs, anticoagulants, and anti-rejection medications.

title: First get outpatient chronic disease certification, then register for cross-regional medical care — hypertension, diabetes, cancer radiotherapy/chemotherapy, dialysis, and anti-rejection treatment can then be covered by yibao across regions
cost_desc: No cost at all. You can complete the cross-regional medical registration once, right from your phone, via the yibao app before you travel.
benefit_desc: According to official documents from the National Healthcare Security Administration, this system is now largely in place. The exact wording reads: “Cross-regional direct settlement of outpatient expenses for five chronic conditions — hypertension, diabetes, radiotherapy/chemotherapy for malignant tumors, dialysis for uremia, and anti-rejection treatment after organ transplants — is now largely accessible at the county level.” “Accessible at the county level” means this service is available county-wide. The documents also mention plans to add five more conditions to this list in the future.
plain_terms: Patients with hypertension, diabetes, outpatient radiotherapy/chemotherapy for malignant tumors, dialysis for uremia, and anti-rejection treatment after organ transplants can now use their yibao coverage for outpatient care anywhere in the country. They won’t need to pay out-of-pocket first and then seek reimbursement back home. However, this only works if they first obtain outpatient chronic disease certification in their home region, then register for cross-regional medical care. Both steps are required for it to take effect.
notes: Both steps are mandatory: first get outpatient chronic disease certification in your home region, then register for cross-regional medical care. Progress on adding those five new conditions varies by region; exact details are determined by local healthcare security authorities.

title: Follow the intervals recommended by your doctor for follow‑up visits, and record every measurement in the same notebook.
cost_desc: Each checkup costs anywhere from a few dozen to several hundred yuan. A trip to the hospital and waiting for results also takes some time. The main difficulty is that you must go regularly, which can easily be put off.
benefit_desc: What matters for chronic conditions is how these values change over time. Keeping them all in one spot also means you won’t have to redo tests or spend extra money when you change medical providers.
plain_terms: For chronic diseases, it’s the trends over time that matter, not any single measurement. Write down the date, the measurement, the medication you’re taking, and its dosage in one place. When you switch doctors, you can show this record so you won’t need to repeat tests or pay for them again.
notes: Be sure to record at least four items each time: the date, the measurement value, the medication being used, and its dosage. Taking a photo of the lab report with your phone works just as well. The key is to keep everything in the same place rather than scattering it across multiple notes.

title: Don’t stop proper treatment to try folk remedies or supplements
cost_desc: No cost at all; you even save money you’d otherwise spend on supplements. It takes no extra time. The hard part is resisting repeated pressure from others to give it a try.
benefit_desc: The dangers of discontinuing treatment are clear, while the advantages of folk remedies remain unproven. This book lists several common types of ineffective supplements in Chapter 6.
plain_terms: The risks of stopping treatment are well known, while the benefits of folk remedies and supplements are uncertain. This means trading a definite harm for an uncertain gain. If you want to try supplements, talk to your doctor first. Some supplements can alter blood levels of anticoagulants and anti-rejection drugs.
notes: Always consult your doctor before trying any supplements. Certain supplements may interact with prescription medications, affecting concentrations of anticoagulants and anti-rejection drugs in the bloodstream.

title: For patients with stable chronic conditions, community clinics can issue up to 12 weeks’ worth of medication at one time
cost_desc: There is no cost involved. Simply ask at your local community health center whether they can issue a long-term prescription.
benefit_desc: Patients no longer need to make monthly trips to larger hospitals just to obtain prescriptions. In the same insurance region, reimbursement rates at community clinics are generally roughly 10 percentage points higher than at higher-tier hospitals.
plain_terms: Individuals whose conditions remain stable and whose medication regimens have not changed can obtain enough medication for 12 weeks from a community health center in one visit. This eliminates the need to travel to a larger hospital each month just to get a prescription and wait in line. Within the same insurance region, reimbursement rates at community-level clinics are typically about 10 percentage points higher than those at higher-tier hospitals.
notes: Whether a patient meets the criteria is determined by the physician; generally, this applies to individuals with a confirmed diagnosis and a stable medication regimen. The actual medication remains the same; what is saved is the time and cost of monthly trips to the hospital and associated fees. If a specific medication is unavailable at a community clinic, patients can inquire about medication shortage registries and delivery services. The same policy also calls for tertiary hospitals to gradually reduce routine outpatient services for such chronic conditions, with those services being transferred to community clinics instead. Relying on larger hospitals solely for prescription refills will become increasingly difficult in the future.

title: Before signing up for a family doctor in your community, find out which services are covered by yibao and which you’ll have to pay for out of pocket
cost_desc: There’s no cost involved. Asking a few questions before you sign up takes just a minute.
benefit_desc: The basic service package is paid for by yibao per regulations. Customized packages require full out‑of‑pocket payment and must also be registered with the county‑level health authority.
plain_terms: The standard package of basic services is covered by yibao as required. Any customized service packages must be paid for entirely by the patient. When someone offers an “upgrade package,” be sure to ask whether it’s a basic or customized package, whether it’s officially registered, and how much it costs per year.
notes: The real value of signing up lies in having a doctor follow your health over the long term, not in the number of services included. When offered an “upgrade package,” ask three key questions: is it a basic or customized package, is it registered, and what’s the annual cost?

title: Get a dilated eye exam right after a diabetes diagnosis, then follow your doctor’s recommended schedule; check your feet once a year.
cost_desc: A single dilated eye exam costs anywhere from a few dozen to several hundred yuan. Foot exams are usually included in routine outpatient visits, so they don’t incur extra charges. The real challenge is remembering to get these checks done even when neither your eyes nor feet feel any discomfort.
benefit_desc: Retinal damage caused by diabetes is known as diabetic retinopathy, while damage to the feet is called diabetic foot disease. Both conditions rarely show any symptoms until they reach an advanced stage. Detecting them early gives patients a much better chance of effective treatment. Once vision is lost or foot ulcers develop, it’s usually too late to reverse the damage.
plain_terms: Diabetes can damage both the retina and feet, but there are almost no noticeable symptoms until the damage becomes severe enough to cause vision loss or foot ulcers. Early detection makes treatment possible. For type 2 diabetes, a dilated eye exam should be done right after diagnosis; for type 1 diabetes, it’s recommended to start five years after onset. If previous tests showed no issues and blood sugar levels remain well-controlled, the interval can be extended to once every one or two years. Foot checks should be done annually.
notes: Type 2 diabetics should get a dilated eye exam right after diagnosis; type 1 diabetics should start five years after onset. The difference exists because type 2 diabetes often develops gradually over several years without obvious signs. If previous tests showed no problems and blood sugar stays under control, the interval can be extended to once every one to two years. People who notice reduced sensation in their feet should inspect the soles daily, even using a mirror if needed.

title: People who have had kidney stones should drink 2.5–3 liters of water daily and keep salt intake under 6 grams
cost_desc: There is no cost at all. Simply make drinking water a daily habit. On days when you sweat a lot, you’ll need even more water — the hard part is remembering to do this every day.
benefit_desc: This is a five-year randomized controlled trial involving 199 patients with idiopathic calcium stones — meaning no underlying cause could be identified. Participants were split into two groups: one group drank at least 2 liters of water daily, while the other received no special intervention. After five years, 12.1% of the water-drinking group had a recurrence, versus 27.0% in the control group (P=0.008). A lower P value indicates a less likely chance that this difference occurred by random chance. The average time to recurrence was 38.7±13.2 months for the water group versus 25.1±16.4 months for the control group (P=0.016). Baseline 24-hour urine volume measurements showed that stone patients produced significantly less urine than healthy individuals: men produced 1,057±238 mL versus 1,401±562 mL in healthy men (P<0.0001), and women produced 990±230 mL versus 1,239±440 mL (P<0.001). NICE guideline NG118, section 1.8.1, offers several recommendations: adults should drink 2.5–3 liters daily, while children and teens should drink 1–2 liters based on age. Adding fresh lemon juice to water is encouraged, and carbonated drinks should be avoided. Adults must also keep daily salt intake under 6 grams.
plain_terms: Roughly one in four people who have had a kidney stone will develop another one within five years. In a study of 199 people who had just experienced their first calcium stone episode, one group was instructed to drink enough water every day. Over five years, 12% of this group had a recurrence, compared to 27% of the control group that received no special instructions. UK guidelines recommend drinking 2.5–3 liters of water daily while keeping salt intake under 6 grams.
notes: This measure reduces recurrence rates by roughly 55% at zero cost, making it the most cost-effective recommendation in this section according to our ranking criteria. The key metric to monitor is 24-hour urine volume, which should reach at least 2–2.5 liters — not simply the amount of water you drink. People who sweat heavily or work in hot environments need to drink even more. This trial involved only patients experiencing their first idiopathic calcium stone episode; different types of stones — such as uric acid, infection-related, or cystine stones — require different treatment approaches. Anyone with a history of kidney stones should undergo a stone composition analysis and a 24-hour urine test to determine whether medication is needed. Do not cut calcium intake to prevent stones; see section 6, item 21 for more details. Severe flank or abdominal pain during a stone episode requires immediate medical attention — drinking more water alone will not resolve it. Non-painful blood in the urine may indicate other conditions; see section 1, item 27 for further information. 〔100〕 〔100〕

title: Long‑term use of uric‑acid‑lowering drugs after a gout diagnosis to keep levels below 360 µmol/L
cost_desc: Allopurinol costs only a few to several tens of yuan per month. At first, blood uric‑acid levels must be checked every few weeks to adjust the dose; once stable, checks can be done every few months. For the first 3–6 months, a second medication to prevent flare‑ups is also required. The difficulty lies in the fact that patients must keep taking it even when they feel no pain.
benefit_desc: In a randomized controlled trial of 517 adults who had experienced gout attacks within the previous 12 months, one group received nurse‑led education and dose adjustments to achieve the target level, while the other continued routine care. After two years, 95 % of the intervention group versus 30 % of the control group had uric‑acid levels below 360 µmol/L (6 mg/dL). The odds of success were 3.18 times higher in the intervention group (RR 3.18, 95 % CI 2.42–4.18; P < 0.0001). Secondary outcomes — attack frequency, tophus formation, and quality of life — also improved. Each additional quality‑adjusted life year gained cost £5,066. Follow‑up data showed that 82 % of participants reported zero attacks in the previous year, versus a median of one attack for the control group (P < 0.001). The proportion still on therapy was 1.19 times higher in the intervention group (adjusted RR 1.19, 1.09–1.30). The 2020 American College of Rheumatology guidelines recommend uric‑acid‑lowering therapy for patients with tophi, bone erosion on imaging, or ≥2 attacks per year; the target is <6 mg/dL, achieved by regular monitoring and dose titration, with allopurinol as first‑line therapy, especially for those with stage 3 or higher chronic kidney disease. Anti‑inflammatory prophylaxis is advised for 3–6 months at initiation. Observational data indicate that after successful control, many patients can discontinue medication without relapse; however, only 13 % remained flare‑free over five years. Alcohol restriction lowers uric‑acid levels by 1.6 mg/dL, while a single beer raises them by 0.16 mg/dL; healthier diets have far smaller effects. Debate persists over optimal drug choice: allopurinol is favored for its efficacy, safety, and low cost, though patients with cardiovascular disease or recent events may be switched to other agents per FDA warnings. The CARES trial linked allopurinol to a 22 % higher risk of all‑cause mortality (HR 1.22) and a 34 % higher risk of cardiovascular death (HR 1.34) versus allopurinol; the European FAST trial found no such increase. Urine alkalinization is not recommended for uricosuric agents due to lack of evidence. Adequate hydration is essential, especially for patients with kidney stones or advanced CKD.
plain_terms: Gout requires lifelong use of uric‑acid‑lowering drugs to keep levels under 360 µmol/L; painkillers alone are insufficient. In a study where nurses helped patients adjust their dose based on lab results, 95 % reached the target after two years, compared with only 30 % of patients seen by regular doctors. Even after reaching the target, medication must not be stopped. Diet changes alone cannot bring levels down to this point, and abstaining from alcohol lowers them by just 1.6 mg/dL.
notes: Controversy exists: different countries recommend different first‑line drugs. The U.S. guideline favors allopurinol and advises avoiding febuxostat in patients with cardiovascular disease, whereas the FAST trial found no increased risk with febuxostat. Probenecid, another uricosuric agent, is available in China. Chinese guidelines (2019 and 2024 updates) provide separate recommendations on drug selection and urine alkalinization; they suggest that sodium bicarbonate may be unnecessary, but hydration remains crucial. Han Chinese individuals should be screened for HLA‑B*5801 before starting allopurinol; carriers account for 7.4 % of Han Chinese, 0.7 % of Caucasians and Hispanics, and have a three‑fold higher risk of allopurinol‑induced hypersensitivity syndrome, a potentially fatal condition involving extensive skin peeling. The 2020 ACR guidelines recommend screening for these groups. Initiation of therapy can temporarily increase flare‑ups, so anti‑inflammatory prophylaxis for 3–6 months is mandatory; discontinuing uric‑acid‑lowering drugs because of pain is a common cause of treatment failure. When an attack occurs, additional anti‑inflammatory medication should be added per medical advice, not the uric‑acid‑lowering drug. Target levels are expressed as <6 mg/dL (≈360 µmol/L); Chinese labs typically report µmol/L. Asymptomatic hyperuricemia is addressed separately in Section 6, Item 19. Sugar‑sweetened beverages and alcohol are discussed in Section 2, Items 7 and 19.

title: For individuals with a history of gout, avoid consuming large single-meal portions of meat and seafood during barbecues and banquets, and strictly limit alcohol
cost_desc: Zero financial outlay. Simply order fewer skewers of meat and seafood dishes, and minimize alcoholic beverages during social dinners. The difficulty is exerting dietary discipline at social dining tables.
benefit_desc: A 1-year prospective internet-based case-crossover study of 633 gout patients compared dietary intake during the 2-day period preceding an acute gout flare with flare-free control periods in the same individuals. Purines are natural chemical compounds in food metabolized into serum uric acid. Dividing total 2-day purine intake into quintiles revealed that compared with the lowest quintile, the subsequent four quintiles showed odds ratios of recurrent gout attacks of 1.17, 1.38, 2.21, and 4.76 respectively (P for trend < 0.001). For animal purines alone, odds ratios were 1.42, 1.34, 1.77, and 2.41. For plant-derived purines, odds ratios were 1.12, 0.99, 1.32, and 1.39. Subgroup analyses stratified by sex, alcohol consumption, diuretic use, allopurinol therapy, NSAID use, and colchicine prophylaxis yielded consistent findings. A companion study of 724 gout patients evaluated alcohol intake within 24 hours prior to flares: compared with zero alcohol, 1 to 2 drinks increased recurrence risk by 36% (OR 1.36, 95% CI: 1.00–1.88) and 2 to 4 drinks increased risk by 51% (OR 1.51, 95% CI: 1.09–2.09), with risk increasing across wine, beer, and distilled spirits. In incident gout, a 12-year prospective cohort study of 47,150 male health professionals demonstrated that the highest quintile of meat consumption had a 41% higher risk of developing gout than the lowest quintile (RR 1.41, 95% CI: 1.07–1.86), and seafood had a 51% higher risk (RR 1.51, 95% CI: 1.17–1.95), while high dairy consumption reduced risk by 44% (RR 0.56, 95% CI: 0.42–0.74). In the same cohort, each additional 12 oz (355 mL) can of beer per day increased incident gout risk by 49% (RR 1.49, 95% CI: 1.32–1.70), and spirits increased risk by 15% per drink daily (RR 1.15, 95% CI: 1.04–1.28).
plain_terms: For individuals with prior gout attacks, consuming high-purine meals over a two-day period raises the odds of an acute recurrent gout attack nearly 5-fold compared to low-purine days, even while taking uric-acid-lowering medications. Consuming two to four alcoholic drinks in the preceding 24 hours raises attack risk by ~50%, across beer, liquor, and wine alike.
notes: Directed primarily at individuals with established gout flares. In individuals without gout, dietary purine intake has a much smaller impact on baseline serum uric acid than commonly believed: in 16,760 white adults without gout, diet explained less than 0.3% of variance in serum urate, whereas common genetic variants explained 23.9%. Thus, while high-purine dining triggers acute attacks, underlying genetic predisposition dominates disease onset. These studies evaluated total purine and ethanol intake rather than cooking technique (cold seafood with beer triggers identical risks to grilled skewers). Dietary restraint cannot replace uric-acid-lowering pharmacotherapy (see Chapter 16, Rule 9). Reducing processed meat and alcohol for cardiovascular mortality is detailed in Chapter 2, Rules 18 and 19.

title: If testing positive for Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), undergo liver ultrasound plus serum AFP screening every six months: initiate antiviral therapy upon physician evaluation and never discontinue medication autonomously
cost_desc: Low cost. Visit hepatology or infectious disease outpatient clinics twice a year for routine blood draws and abdominal sonography; centralized volume-based procurement (VBP) in China has reduced annual generic entecavir antiviral medication expenses to just over 100 RMB. The difficulty is adhering to biannual surveillance and daily long-term oral medication while completely asymptomatic.
benefit_desc: In a randomized controlled trial in Shanghai involving 18,816 individuals aged 35–59 with chronic HBV infection or history of chronic hepatitis, the screening arm was invited for biannual AFP and ultrasound examinations, while the control arm received routine care without screening.
