If the pre‑termination examination is not performed, the employer cannot terminate or end your contract.
notes: During an interview, asking just three questions can help you gauge whether a company is legitimate: whether the job involves occupational hazards, whether these are mentioned in the contract, and who pays for the pre‑employment health check. If the interviewer cannot answer or suggests “just start working first,” proceed with caution. The requirement for a pre‑termination health examination is a crucial safeguard — without it, the employer cannot end your contract. This examination also serves as key evidence for any future occupational disease claim; the same applies to the health records copy you must obtain before leaving. Claims for occupational disease are handled as work‑related injuries, and the corresponding benefits are outlined from item 12 onward.

title: Damage caused by dust, noise, and chemical toxins is irreversible: employers must provide protective gear, and workers can refuse unsafe tasks
cost_desc: No monetary cost. The real challenge is consistently wearing respirators, earplugs, and safety goggles, as well as refusing to perform tasks lacking adequate protection — this may lead coworkers to label you as “too picky.”
benefit_desc: As of August 1, 2025, the official list of occupational diseases comprises 12 main categories containing 135 distinct conditions, including four open-ended clauses. Pneumoconiosis ranks first among them, covering silicosis, coal worker’s pneumoconiosis, graphite pneumoconiosis, carbon black pneumoconiosis, asbestosis, talc pneumoconiosis, cement pneumoconiosis, mica pneumoconiosis, potter’s pneumoconiosis, aluminum pneumoconiosis, welder’s pneumoconiosis, and foundry worker’s pneumoconiosis, plus one additional open clause. Noise-induced hearing loss and blast-induced hearing loss fall under occupational ear, nose, throat, and oral diseases; chemical eye burns and photic keratitis are listed under occupational eye diseases. All these injuries are permanent — once damaged, lungs and hearing cannot be repaired. Four fundamental rights are legally guaranteed: first, the right to be informed about all occupational hazards present, their potential consequences, and required protective measures; second, the right to demand provision of compliant protective equipment and improved working conditions; third, the right to report, criticize, or file complaints against any violations of occupational health laws or practices endangering health; fourth, the right to refuse any directive ordering work without proper protective measures. Furthermore, any employer action — such as wage cuts, benefit reductions, or contract termination — taken solely because a worker exercised these lawful rights is legally void nationwide.
plain_terms: Pneumoconiosis, noise-induced hearing loss, and chemical eye burns are all listed as statutory occupational diseases. Once lung tissue or hearing is damaged, there is no treatment capable of restoring it. You have the right to know exactly what hazards exist at your workplace and to demand that your employer supply protective equipment and facilities. You may refuse any job that fails to provide these safeguards. Any attempt by your employer to cut your pay or terminate your contract in retaliation for exercising these rights is legally invalid.
notes: Ensure you use respirators specifically rated for particulate filtration; ordinary gauze masks or disposable surgical masks offer no protection against dust. If your employer does not supply earplugs for noisy environments, purchasing them yourself is advisable, as hearing loss cannot be reversed. The belief that “working just two years to save money is safe” does not apply to pneumoconiosis — silicosis can manifest years after exposure ends and may worsen over time, making off-duty health checks essential (see Rule 9 of this section, which mandates three free occupational health examinations paid for by employers). The updated list also includes two new categories: occupational musculoskeletal disorders, specifically carpal tunnel syndrome affecting manufacturing workers performing repetitive wrist motions; and occupational mental and behavioral disorders, specifically post-traumatic stress disorder affecting police officers, medical personnel, and emergency responders involved in crisis response. Immediate first-aid measures for chemical splashes onto skin are detailed in item 13, clause 21.

title: If you’re injured at work or hit while commuting, the first step is to get a work‑injury determination; if your employer won’t file it, you must do it yourself.
cost_desc: There is no cost — just a trip to the social insurance authority. You’ll need three documents: a work‑injury determination application form, proof of employment, and a medical diagnosis certificate.
benefit_desc: Without a work‑injury determination, all related benefits disappear: medical care, wage continuation while you recover, and disability payments. If an employer misses the 30‑day deadline, it must pay all required benefits out of its own funds.
plain_terms: Injuries that happen at work are considered work‑related injuries. Being hit while commuting — provided you bear no significant fault — also qualifies as a work‑injury. Without a formal work‑injury determination, however, you won’t receive medical coverage, wage replacement during recovery, or disability benefits. Employers must file the application within 30 days; if they fail to do so, you, your family, or a labor union may file it within one year.
notes: The one‑year deadline is absolute — after that you can’t apply. The burden of proof rests with the employer: if it denies that an injury is work‑related, it must provide evidence to the contrary. Still, you should keep your own records — photos from the scene, coworkers’ contact info, medical records, and attendance logs. Article 16 lists three situations where injuries are not considered work‑related: intentional criminal acts, intoxication or drug use, and self‑inflicted harm or suicide. Article 15 also defines “deemed work‑injuries”: death from a sudden illness at work or within 48 hours after unsuccessful emergency treatment.

title: Don’t believe the myth that “staying at work counts as a workplace injury”: if you suddenly feel unwell, call 120 first — don’t rush to clock in.
cost_desc: No cost at all.
benefit_desc: This rule states that a worker must suffer a sudden illness during working hours at their workplace, and then die within 48 hours despite medical efforts, to be deemed a workplace injury. Delaying medical care just to meet these conditions means sacrificing your own chance of survival for compensation that you might not even receive.
plain_terms: Hurrying to the office when you suddenly feel unwell won’t earn you any extra compensation. To be classified as a workplace injury, the incident must occur during working hours and at the workplace; if it happens on the way to work before you even arrive, it doesn’t qualify. Cases where medical treatment is delayed past 48 hours also don’t count. Those few extra minutes spent trying to meet the criteria can actually lower your chances of survival.
notes: Both conditions must be met: the illness must occur during working hours and at the workplace. It does not apply if the illness strikes on the way to work before reaching the office. If a worker falls ill at work, is taken home or to hospital, and dies within 48 hours despite treatment, this rule may still apply. What matters most is where the person was at the moment of illness, not where they ultimately die. Some short videos wrongly claim that “staying at work guarantees compensation”; in reality, those crucial first few minutes after falling ill — when prompt medical care is sought — are what truly determine the outcome. Additionally, the 48‑hour limit is strict: any case where treatment is delayed beyond this period does not qualify.

title: Even if the employer fails to enroll you in workers’ compensation insurance, you still qualify for full benefits paid entirely by the employer at the same rates
cost_desc: There’s no direct cost to you. However, if the employer refuses to comply, you’ll need to pursue arbitration or even litigation, which can take several months. The difficulty lies in having to stay actively involved throughout this lengthy process.
benefit_desc: Statutory rules clearly state that when an employer neglects to enroll an employee in workers’ compensation insurance, any resulting workplace injuries must be compensated by that employer itself, using identical coverage items and payment amounts mandated by law. In other words, the employer bears the entire financial burden without exception.
plain_terms: Even if your employer does not enroll you in workers’ compensation insurance, you are still entitled to all related benefits. Those benefits must then be paid in full by the employer, using the same coverage items and payment standards as if insurance had been purchased. Failure to enroll is penalized: the employer must retroactively pay premiums plus a daily late fee of 0.05%, and may face fines equal to 1–3 times the unpaid amount. The claim “the company can’t compensate you because it didn’t buy insurance” is simply untrue.
notes: “The company can’t pay compensation because it didn’t purchase workers’ compensation insurance” is one of the most common false statements encountered in such cases. While non‑enrollment brings penalties for the employer, it does not reduce your right to receive full compensation.

title: After injuries stabilize, undergo a work capacity assessment; disability grades translate directly into compensation
cost_desc: There is no monetary cost. However, completing the work capacity assessment process takes some time.
benefit_desc: One-time disability benefits are paid out as a lump sum, calculated based on the individual’s own salary and their disability grade. For Grade 5, this equals 18 months’ salary; for Grade 6, 16 months’; for Grade 7, 13 months’; for Grade 8, 11 months’; for Grade 9, 9 months’; and for Grade 10, 7 months’.
plain_terms: Once injuries have stabilized, a work capacity assessment can be done, and the resulting disability grade translates directly into compensation. One-time disability benefits are calculated based on the individual’s own salary: Grade 5 equals 18 months’ salary, Grade 6 equals 16 months’, Grade 7 equals 13 months’, Grade 8 equals 11 months’, Grade 9 equals 9 months’, and Grade 10 equals 7 months’. Before the assessment results are finalized, do not sign any “one-time settlement” agreements.
notes: Workers with Grades 5 and 6 retain their employment status and continue to receive disability allowances each month from their employer. For those with Grades 7 through 10, upon contract expiration or voluntary termination, two additional payments apply: a one-time work injury medical allowance paid by the fund, and a one-time disability employment allowance paid by the employer; exact amounts are set by provincial regulations. Before the assessment results are finalized, do not sign any “one-time settlement” agreements.

title: Three types of compensation for work-related deaths: funeral allowance, survivor’s pension, and one-time death benefit
cost_desc: No cost involved; only a set of administrative procedures are required.
benefit_desc: Three separate payments are provided for work-related deaths. First, the funeral allowance equals six months of the average monthly wage of workers in the relevant regional insurance pool. Second, the survivor’s pension is paid monthly at rates set relative to the deceased worker’s wage: 40% for the spouse, 30% for each other eligible dependent. Third, the one-time death benefit is a single nationwide amount equal to 20 times the per capita disposable income of urban residents in China from the previous year, with no regional variations. For deaths occurring in 2026, this benefit totals roughly 1.13 million yuan (1,130,040 yuan), calculated as 56,502 yuan — the prior year’s per capita disposable income for urban residents — multiplied by 20.
plain_terms: There are three distinct payments related to work-related deaths — don’t focus on just one of them. The funeral allowance equals six months of the average monthly wage of local workers from the previous year. The survivor’s pension is paid monthly based on the deceased worker’s wage: 40% goes to the spouse, while other eligible dependents each receive 30% of that wage. The one-time death benefit is a fixed amount nationwide: it equals 20 times the per capita disposable income of urban residents across China in the prior year.
notes: The one-time death benefit is standardized nationwide, and its exact amount updates each year based on data released by China’s National Bureau of Statistics. When negotiating compensation, claims citing “lower local standards in our region” are not valid.

title: If you’ve been bullied, insulted, or mistreated at work for a long time, don’t just endure it: document everything as evidence, then take action based on the nature of the abuse.
cost_desc: There’s no monetary cost. However, it does take time to record details such as dates, witnesses, exact quotes from the abuser, and to keep original screenshots and emails. Legal proceedings like arbitration or lawsuits can last several months. Changing jobs is the most costly option; you must weigh these factors yourself.
benefit_desc: From a health perspective: three Swedish and Danish cohorts comprising 79,201 working adults aged 18–65 were studied over an average of 12.4 years. At baseline, none had cardiovascular disease; 9% reported having experienced workplace bullying in the previous year. Those who endured bullying faced a 59% higher risk of developing cardiovascular disease (coronary heart disease or cerebrovascular disease; HR 1.59, 95% CI 1.28–1.98). Individuals subjected to workplace violence faced a 25% higher risk (HR 1.25, 95% CI 1.12–1.40); both risks increased with the frequency of abuse. A Norwegian nationwide survey of 1,846 workers, followed over three rounds of testing spaced two to three years apart, found that bullied individuals were roughly twice as likely to develop suicidal thoughts (OR 2.05, 95% CI 1.08–3.89). Conversely, people with prior suicidal thoughts did not later become more prone to bullying. From a legal standpoint: China currently lacks specific legislation addressing “workplace bullying”; actions must be evaluated against existing laws. Employers found guilty of insults, corporal punishment, physical assault, unlawful searches, or unlawful detention of workers face administrative penalties and must compensate for any harm; criminal acts incur further legal consequences. If an employer uses violence or threats to compel work, employees may terminate their contracts immediately without notice and are entitled to financial compensation. Employers must also implement measures to prevent and curb sexual harassment by leveraging authority or hierarchical relationships; victims may seek civil redress from harassers. Labor arbitration cases are resolved within 45 days of acceptance, with a possible extension of 15 days for complex cases.
plain_terms: Employees who experience workplace bullying have a roughly 60% higher risk of developing heart disease or having a stroke, and this risk rises with the severity of the bullying. After several years, they are also about twice as likely to entertain suicidal thoughts compared to their peers. Being constantly insulted and mistreated is far from a minor inconvenience that can simply be “tolerated.”
notes: This grade is assigned because the health data derive from observational studies rather than randomized controlled trials, and “bullying” was self-reported by participants. This guidance does not advocate quitting a job at the first sign of mistreatment; the personal cost of changing jobs must be considered. Four practical steps can be taken: first, begin documenting incidents immediately; refer to Section 8, Item 41 for guidance on recording audio evidence. Second, submit written complaints through official internal channels and retain proof of such submissions. Third, if physical assault, unlawful confinement, or public humiliation occurs, contact law enforcement. Fourth, if forced to leave due to unpaid wages or lack of social insurance contributions, follow Section 7 (“Do not voluntarily resign”) and Section 8 (“Preserve evidence prior to leaving”) of this chapter. For details on calculating compensation, see Section 4 (“Calculate your entitlements after layoffs”). Mere neglect, exclusion, or minor mistreatment rarely violate any specific statutes; in such cases, internal complaints, job transfers, or changing employers are the primary remedies. Arbitration proceedings may take up to 60 days, while civil lawsuits typically require at least six months; legal fees must be borne by the plaintiff. If the situation becomes unbearable, call 12356 as outlined in Section 1, Item 25.

title: When you leave a job, ask the employer for a termination certificate stating contract term, separation date, position, and years of service
cost_desc: No cost. Ask in person before you go, or send a written message and keep proof you asked. The hard part is asking when relations are bad. If the employer stalls, complaints or arbitration can take weeks to months.
benefit_desc: The Labor Contract Law requires the employer to issue a certificate when the contract is terminated or ended. The rule does not depend on who initiated it — non-renewal, resignation, or dismissal all count. The employer must also complete personnel file and social insurance transfer within 15 days. The implementing regulations require four items on the certificate: contract term, date of termination or end, job position, and years of service at the unit. The Unemployment Insurance Regulations require laid-off workers to take the employer’s certificate to the social insurance agency promptly for unemployment registration. Unemployment benefits start from the date of unemployment registration. If the employer does not issue a written certificate, the labor administration orders correction. If you suffer loss, the employer must pay damages. The law also provides that a new employer who hires someone still bound to a former employer and causes loss to the former employer bears joint and several liability. The termination certificate is written proof that you and the former employer have ended the relationship (nationwide).
plain_terms: Whether you were dismissed, the contract expired, or you resigned, the employer must give you a termination certificate when you leave and transfer your personnel file and social insurance within 15 days. The certificate must state contract term, separation date, position, and how many years you worked there. You need it for unemployment registration. If the employer refuses, labor authorities order correction and must compensate any loss they caused.
notes: The law does not tie issuing the certificate to completing handover; economic compensation is paid after handover is done. If the employer drags its feet, send one more written demand. If still no certificate, call 12333 or complain to labor inspection at the human resources bureau. Complaints are free; after a case is opened, investigation must finish within 60 working days, extendable 30 days for complex cases. To claim damages from the employer, use labor arbitration — also free — within one year. After acceptance, arbitration closes within 45 days, extendable 15 days. You must prove the loss yourself, for example delayed unemployment registration or a new employer refusing you for lack of proof. If you disagree with the award, go to court; ordinary first-instance procedure starts at six months. Labor dispute court fees are 10 yuan per case; attorney fees are not litigation costs and you pay yourself. The four required items do not include reason for leaving. If the certificate says “voluntary resignation for personal reasons” and that is false, object on the spot — see this section item 7 (do not sign voluntary resignation). How to claim unemployment insurance: Section 7, item 1.

title: Before spending severance pay, check individual income tax: amounts within three times the local prior-year average employee wage are tax-free; the excess is taxed separately, not merged into that year’s salary
cost_desc: No cost. Look up the local prior-year average employee wage, then spend a few minutes checking how the employer withheld tax. The individual income tax app shows line-by-line filing for each payment.
benefit_desc: A Ministry of Finance and State Taxation Administration circular states that one-time compensation income from terminating a labor relationship with an employer — including economic compensation, living allowances, and other subsidies — is exempt from individual income tax within three times the local prior-year average employee wage. The portion above three times is not merged into annual comprehensive income; it is taxed separately under the comprehensive income rate table. That table taxes annual amounts up to 36,000 yuan at 3%, 36,000 to 144,000 yuan at 10%, and higher brackets up to 45%. Example: if the local prior-year average employee wage is 100,000 yuan, three times is 300,000 yuan. On 360,000 yuan compensation, only the 60,000 yuan excess is taxed — 3,480 yuan. If the full 360,000 yuan were taxed under that table, tax would be 58,080 yuan. Effective 1 January 2019; no end date stated (nationwide).
plain_terms: One-time compensation from ending an employment relationship is tax-free up to three times the local prior-year average employee wage. Amounts above that are taxed on their own, not added to your annual comprehensive income. If the employer lumped the whole payment into monthly wages and withheld tax that way, ask the employer first, then call 12366 for the tax bureau.
notes: The same circular sets an end date for the annual one-time bonus policy, later extended to 31 December 2027. The termination-compensation rule has no end date and does not follow the bonus extension. The circular names economic compensation, living allowances, and other subsidies; it does not separately name payment in lieu of notice or damages for unlawful termination. If unsure whether those count, call 12366 locally. Which figure counts as “local prior-year average employee wage” is determined by the local tax bureau. How compensation is calculated: this section item 4 (calculate N when laid off), item 5 (no 30-day notice), item 6 (damages for unlawful termination). One-time subsidies for early retirement or internal retirement use a different formula and are not covered here.

title: When changing cities for work: Transfer your pension and basic medical insurance accounts to the new locality so contribution years accumulate continuously, and do not surrender coverage
cost_desc: Zero monetary cost. After enrolling and contributing in the new location, submit a transfer application through your new employer or independently, either online or at a public administrative service desk. Pension transfers take several dozen working days end-to-end, while medical insurance transfers require approximately 15 working days.
benefit_desc: The Social Insurance Law stipulates that when workers relocate across pooling regions for employment, their basic pension insurance accounts follow them, and contribution years accumulate cumulatively. The same rule applies to employee basic medical insurance: coverage accounts transfer and contribution durations accumulate continuously. At retirement, pensions are calculated segmented by jurisdiction and disbursed through a unified payout channel. Interprovincial pension transfers follow State Council interim procedures: prior to reaching statutory pension entitlement age, pension relations cannot be terminated or refunded, and personal accounts cannot be withdrawn early. The entire principal and accrued interest of the employee's personal account are transferred. For the employer pooling portion, funds equal to 12% of the employee's actual wage base for each year after 1998 are transferred to the incoming jurisdiction. Pension disbursements are calculated based on historical wage bases, cumulative contribution years, and local average wages at the final disbursement jurisdiction. Procedurally, once enrolled and contributing in the new city, submit an application to the receiving social insurance agency. The receiving office audits within 15 working days; upon receipt of the acceptance notice, the transferring office executes the transfer within 15 working days; and the receiving office finalizes enrollment within 15 working days of fund arrival. Under State Council "Inter-Provincial Government Services" guidelines, interprovincial transfers are processed entirely through the receiving city's portal without requiring in-person visits to your former city. For employee medical insurance, former coverage must be paused before the new account is activated to initiate transfer. Applications can be submitted online via the National Healthcare Security Administration service platform (fuwu.nhsa.gov.cn) or at local service windows. Outgoing transfer completes within 10 working days, incoming enrollment within 5 working days, and personal account balances transfer in full. If the contribution gap before transfer is within 3 months, retroactive payment waives any waiting period, allowing immediate reimbursement in the month of contribution as well as retroactive reimbursement for the gap period. If the contribution gap exceeds 3 months, local waiting periods apply, capped in principle at 6 months (nationwide).
plain_terms: When relocating between cities for employment, both your pension and employee medical insurance accounts can follow you, allowing cumulative contribution years to stack without restarting. Before reaching statutory retirement age, you cannot cancel your pension insurance to cash out funds. If medical insurance contributions lapse for more than 3 months, you may face a waiting period of up to 6 months before medical expenses can be reimbursed in the new location, so avoid extended gaps between jobs.
notes: If moving across provincial borders to a non-registered household (hukou) province when a male worker reaches age 50 or a female worker reaches age 40, original pension relations remain anchored at the previous location; the new locality opens a temporary contribution account recording all unit and personal payments. The statutory priority rule determining final retirement payout location is as follows: if anchored in the household registration province, benefits are drawn at the household locality; if residing elsewhere and cumulative contributions at the active account exceed 10 years, benefits are drawn locally; if under 10 years, relations roll back to the most recent jurisdiction where contributions exceeded 10 years; if no locality reaches 10 years, all funds aggregate to the household registration province. Pension benefit formulas use the local average wage of the final payout jurisdiction. Intraprovincial intercity transfer guidelines are established by individual provincial governments. Individuals already receiving monthly pensions cannot transfer accounts. For calculating contribution gaps and eligibility prerequisites, see Chapter 7, Rule 18 (lapsed social security). For flexible employment self-contributions, see Chapter 31, Rule 11.

title: If your employer fails to execute a written employment contract after one month, demand double wages starting from the second month (capped at 11 months); after one year, an open-ended contract is legally established
cost_desc: Zero financial outlay. Preserve evidence of active employment: payroll bank deposits, attendance clock-ins, corporate badges, and work-related chat records. If the employer refuses, file for labor arbitration (free of charge, mandated to conclude within 45 days, extendable by 15 days). Appeals proceed to court; first-instance regular civil procedure takes at least 6 months with personal legal fees. The difficulty is asserting legal claims while remaining employed at the company.
benefit_desc: The Labor Contract Law mandates that employers execute written labor contracts upon establishing employment relationships; if not signed on the first day, contracts must be executed within one month of employment commencement. Where an employer fails to execute a written contract after more than one month but less than one year, it must pay the employee twice their monthly wage. Implementing regulations clarify the exact calculation period: starting on the day following the completion of the first month and ending on the day preceding retroactive contract execution. Where one year has elapsed without a written contract, double wages are payable up to the day before the one-year mark (capped at 11 months of double wages); from the one-year mark onward, an open-ended employment contract is legally deemed established, and the employer must retroactively execute the contract immediately. Under Supreme People's Court judicial interpretations effective September 2025, double wages are calculated monthly (or by actual working days for partial months); employers are exempt from double wages only if they prove non-execution was caused by force majeure or the employee's intentional refusal/gross negligence. If an employee refuses to sign upon written notice during the first month, the employer may terminate employment in writing with zero severance, paying only accrued wages for days worked. Once an open-ended contract is legally established, subsequent claims for double wages are not supported.
plain_terms: If an employer fails to sign a written employment contract after one month of work, they must pay you double monthly wages starting from the second month, up to a maximum of 11 additional months. If a full year passes without a written contract, you are legally deemed to have an open-ended (permanent) employment contract. If the company presents a contract to sign, do not deliberately refuse to sign, as intentional employee obstruction forfeits double wages.
notes: Statutory limitations: under Beijing judicial standards, claims for double wage differentials are subject to a 1-year arbitration statute of limitations, calculated backward by days from the date of application; delaying claims reduces recoverable months. Apply for arbitration promptly while employed or upon departure. If retroactively executing a contract, backdating the effective date to your first day generally extinguishes double-wage claims unless you prove signature under duress. Employer compliance requirements for hiring within the first month are detailed in Chapter 12, Rule 16.

title: If your employer fails to pay or underpays social insurance, lodge an administrative complaint for retroactive back-payments; if resigning over unpaid insurance, specify the statutory violation in your resignation notice to secure statutory severance
cost_desc: Zero financial fee. Audit contribution history via municipal social security apps and save official statement PDFs. To compel back-payments, file an administrative complaint via the 12333 hotline or local labor inspection offices. To claim statutory severance, initiate labor arbitration (free of charge, 45-day statutory timeline). The difficulty is securing subsequent employment income before resigning.
benefit_desc: The Social Insurance Law mandates that employers register, declare, and pay full social insurance contributions on time, prohibiting delays, reductions, or exemptions absent statutory force majeure. If an employer infringes social security rights, employees can demand administrative enforcement from social insurance administrative authorities or collection agencies. Unpaid contributions trigger mandatory cure orders, plus daily late surcharges of 0.05% (5/10,000) from the date of default; failure to rectify within statutory deadlines incurs fines between 1 and 3 times the overdue amount. Labor security inspection bureaus are mandated to conclude investigations within 60 working days (extendable by 30 days for complex matters). Under Article 38 of the Labor Contract Law, if an employer fails to pay social insurance premiums according to law, the employee may terminate the labor contract immediately, and the employer must pay statutory economic compensation (severance). Conversely, resigning with 30 days' advance notice for personal reasons entitles you to zero severance; the written notice must explicitly cite statutory non-compliance. Supreme People's Court judicial interpretations effective September 2025 affirm: agreements between employers and employees waiving social security contributions, or unilateral employee waiver pledges, are legally null and void. Lawsuits demanding statutory severance based on employer social security delinquency shall be supported. If an employer fails to establish social insurance and the social insurance agency cannot process retroactive contributions, causing loss of insurance benefits, employees can sue the employer for consequential damages in labor arbitration.
plain_terms: If an employer fails to pay social insurance or pays under an illegally reduced wage base, you can lodge a labor complaint mandating back-payments plus daily late fees. You can also terminate your labor contract in writing and demand statutory severance (N). Your resignation notice must explicitly cite the employer's failure to pay statutory social security; resigning for "personal reasons" forfeits all severance. Agreements where employees "voluntarily waive social insurance" are legally null and void.
notes: To compel historical back-payments, utilize administrative labor inspection complaints rather than arbitration: judicial consensus holds that direct orders for social security back-payments fall under administrative jurisdiction. Act within statutory enforcement deadlines: labor violations not reported within 2 years are barred from investigation, though ongoing contribution arrears calculate the 2-year window from the date defaults terminate. Underreporting contribution wage bases triggers varying judicial standards: Beijing courts recognize non-compliance only where zero accounts were established in the preceding year or entire statutory insurance tiers were omitted; consult local arbitration tribunals. If an employer previously paid cash allowances in lieu of insurance and subsequently completes retroactive social security payments, it can claw back cash allowances. Workplace injuries occurring without statutory work injury insurance are covered in Chapter 19, Rule 13. Bridging social security lapses is covered in Chapter 7, Rule 18.

title: If your employer demands liquidated damages upon departure, check statutory categories: liquidated damages are legally enforceable ONLY for special training service periods and non-compete agreements
cost_desc: Zero financial outlay. Review your employment contract, specialized training covenants, and non-compete agreements against statutory provisions. If the employer unlawfully docks wages to offset purported liquidated damages, file for labor arbitration (free of charge, 45-day statutory timeline).
benefit_desc: The Labor Contract Law strictly provides that apart from specialized technical training service periods and non-compete restrictions, employers are legally prohibited from stipulating liquidated damages against employees. Under the first exception, where an employer provides specialized funds for professional technical training, it may agree on a service term commitment. If the employee breaches the commitment by leaving early, liquidated damages cannot exceed the total training expenses incurred by the employer, and actual damages cannot exceed the pro-rata portion amortized over the unserved remainder of the agreed service term (e.g. on 30,000 RMB training with a 3-year term, resigning after 2 years caps damages at 10,000 RMB). Training expenses must be substantiated by official payment vouchers, invoices, and direct travel receipts. Furthermore, if the employee terminates the contract due to employer fault (such as unpaid wages or non-payment of social insurance), the employee is not liable for service-period liquidated damages. The second exception is non-compete covenants (see Chapter 11, Rule 12). Clauses exempting employers from statutory responsibilities or depriving employees of basic statutory rights are legally null and void.
plain_terms: Contract clauses stating that "resigning early requires paying penalties" are legally void with only two statutory exceptions: where the employer funded specialized technical training under a service commitment, or under a valid non-compete agreement. Even under specialized training agreements, penalties cannot exceed the actual training expenses and must be amortized against completed service years.
notes: Inability to levy contractual liquidated damages does not mean an employee is immune from tort liability: leaving without 30 days' advance written notice or leaking trade secrets that causes verifiable direct economic losses makes the employee liable for compensatory damages, but the employer bears the evidentiary burden of proving actual losses. Where an employer provided extraordinary benefits like municipal household registration (Hukou) tied to a service period and the employee departs early, courts may award compensatory damages based on actual employer loss, fault, and fulfilled service duration, even while striking down punitive liquidated damages clauses. If an employee is terminated for gross misconduct or criminal acts, service-period liquidated damages remain payable. Recovering illegally docked wages is covered in Chapter 7, Rule 2. Benefit is categorized as Moderate.

title: If your employer unilaterally demotes you or slashes your salary, object in writing immediately: working silently under the new terms for over a month waives your right to invalidate the change
cost_desc: Zero financial cost. Immediately upon receiving demotion or salary cut notices, dispatch a formal written objection via company email or WeChat, preserving screenshots. The difficulty is withstanding face-to-face workplace friction while remaining on the job. If the employer terminates you or unlawfully docks wages, initiate labor arbitration (free of charge, 45-day statutory timeline).
benefit_desc: Under the Labor Contract Law, employment contracts can only be modified if employer and employee reach consensus through negotiation, and amendments must be executed in written form. However, Supreme People's Court judicial interpretations establish a critical exception: where parties orally agree to modify a labor contract and the employee actually performs under the modified terms for more than one month, the modification is legally binding. Courts will not support an employee's subsequent claim that the change was invalid due to lack of written form, provided the modified terms do not violate mandatory laws or public order. Judicial standards issued by Beijing High Court clarify employer management discretion: where contracts do not specify a precise job role, employers may reasonably adjust positions based on legitimate operational needs, evaluated against four criteria: operational necessity, legitimate corporate purpose, employee competency match, and preservation of salary/benefits. Where contracts explicitly define the position without unilateral reassignment clauses, unilateral demotion constitutes contractual breach, requiring back-pay of wage differentials benchmarked against the original role. Broad work location stipulations such as "Nationwide" or "Beijing Municipality" are deemed ambiguous, benchmarking statutory location to where the employee actually reported to work; employers cannot alter work locations without justifiable cause. If an employer fails to pay agreed wages in full and on time, employees can terminate the contract and claim statutory severance.
plain_terms: Modifying job roles or compensation constitutes an amendment to the employment contract, requiring mutual agreement in writing. However, if you remain silent and work under the modified role or reduced salary for over one month, courts legally treat your conduct as tacit acceptance and will reject subsequent claims that the modification was invalid. Object in writing immediately upon notice.
notes: Graded Evidence Grade B because "tacit acceptance after one month" is derived from Judicial Interpretation Article 43 and regional judicial guidelines rather than express statutory wording. After submitting a written objection, continue reporting to work while explicitly stating that attendance is under protest; completely refusing to report to work risks dismissal for job abandonment. If the demotion is subsequently adjudicated unlawful, dismissal constitutes illegal termination subject to double statutory severance (2N, Chapter 19, Rule 6); if the transfer is deemed reasonable, severance is forfeited. If major objective conditions change and parties fail to agree on modifications, employers may terminate contracts with 30 days' advance notice or 1 month's salary in lieu of notice (N+1, Chapter 19, Rule 5). Recovering docked wages is covered in Chapter 7, Rule 2. Benefit is categorized as Moderate.

title: For labor dispatch workers, wages must match permanent staff on identical positions, and both the dispatch agency and host company share joint and several liability for workplace harms
cost_desc: Zero financial cost. Check your employment contract to verify which corporate entity is stamped as your legal employer. The dispatch agency is legally obligated to disclose the terms of the commercial dispatch agreement. If disputes arise, file for labor arbitration (free of charge, 45-day statutory timeline).
benefit_desc: The Labor Contract Law provides that the labor dispatch agency is your statutory employer, mandated to execute fixed-term employment contracts of at least 2 years and pay monthly wages; during unassigned gaps between assignments, the agency must pay monthly wages based on local statutory minimum wage benchmarks. The dispatch agency must disclose dispatch agreements and cannot withhold compensation paid by the host company; neither firm may charge recruitment fees. Dispatched employees enjoy the statutory right to equal pay for equal work: host companies must apply identical remuneration distribution methods for identical positions, or benchmark against local prevailing wages for comparable roles if no direct internal positions exist. Host companies must pay overtime, performance bonuses, and provide role-related welfare benefits without discrimination, adjusting wages normally during continuous assignments. Statutory dispatch is strictly restricted to temporary, auxiliary, or substitutable positions (temporary positions cannot exceed 6 months), and dispatched personnel cannot exceed 10% of total host enterprise workforce. Where host enterprises inflict harm on dispatched workers, the dispatch agency and host enterprise bear joint and several tort liability, meaning you can demand full compensation from either firm and name both as co-respondents in labor arbitration. If an occupational injury occurs at the host entity, the dispatch agency must file for work injury recognition and bear insurance liabilities, with the host company assisting investigations.
plain_terms: As a dispatched agency worker, your employment contract is signed with the labor dispatch agency, but the host company where you work daily shares statutory legal duties. Your wages must be calculated under the identical compensation and incentive structure as direct permanent employees in matching roles. If you suffer damages or injury at the host company, both companies are jointly and severally liable—you can pursue either or both for 100% of compensation. Between client assignments, the agency must pay you monthly statutory minimum wage.
notes: "Equal pay for equal work" mandates applying the identical allocation formulas rather than guaranteeing identical net pay regardless of tenure. If a host company returns you and the dispatch agency proposes new assignments with reduced terms, you may decline and the agency cannot terminate your contract on that basis. Statutory severance upon lawful contract termination is calculated as detailed in Chapter 19, Rule 4. If injured on duty at a host company, demand that the agency file for statutory work injury recognition, or file independently if they refuse (Chapter 19, Rule 11). Recovering unpaid wages is covered in Chapter 7, Rule 2. Benefit is categorized as Moderate.

title: Keep infants sleeping on their backs on a firm surface; share a room but not a bed; and do not place any soft items in the crib or bed.
cost_desc: This costs nothing upfront. However, you’ll need to replace the mattress with a firm one, which may cost several hundred yuan. The real challenge is resisting pressure from older relatives to deviate from this rule.
benefit_desc: Each year, nearly 3,500 infants in the U.S. lose their lives to sleep-related issues, including sudden infant death syndrome, deaths of unknown cause, and accidental suffocation in bedding. The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends a safe sleep environment consisting of: infants sleeping on their backs; using a solid, non-inclined sleeping surface; sharing a room without sharing a bed; and avoiding soft bedding and overheating. Additional protective measures include breastfeeding, keeping infants away from nicotine and alcohol, ensuring all vaccinations are up to date, and offering a pacifier during sleep.
plain_terms: Always place babies on their backs to sleep on a hard, flat surface. Parents and infants should share a room, but not the same bed. Never put pillows, blankets, bed rails, stuffed animals, or special shaped pillows in the sleeping area. Inclined cribs or baby chairs are only meant for sitting — they must never be used as a sleeping surface. In the United States alone, roughly 3,500 infants die each year from sleep-related causes.
notes: “Do not place any soft items in the bed” means absolutely no pillows, blankets, bed rails, stuffed toys, or shaped pillows — even nursing pillows that appear perfectly safe are prohibited. Inclined cribs and baby chairs must never be used as sleeping areas. This requirement represents the biggest departure from common practice in this section, and it often requires the strongest resistance to family pressure.

title: Administer the first dose of hepatitis B vaccine within 24 hours after birth
cost_desc: No cost at all. The hepatitis B vaccine is part of the routine immunization program, so it is provided free of charge. It is given to newborns in the hospital on the day of birth; no extra trips are needed.
benefit_desc: The World Health Organization states: “All infants should receive the hepatitis B vaccine as early as possible after birth, ideally within 24 hours.” The rationale behind this recommendation is that “about 95% of infections in infants and toddlers progress to chronic hepatitis.” Most adults who contract the virus also recover spontaneously, meaning they do not require any treatment to get better.
plain_terms: The first dose of hepatitis B vaccine must be given to a newborn within 24 hours after birth. Roughly 95% of infants and toddlers who contract hepatitis B go on to develop chronic hepatitis. In contrast, the vast majority of adults who get infected recover on their own without medical intervention. Hence, the earlier this vaccine is administered, the greater its protective benefit. If the mother tests positive for hepatitis B surface antigen, the infant also needs to receive an injection of hepatitis B immunoglobulin at the same time.
notes: If the mother tests positive for hepatitis B surface antigen, the newborn must receive an injection of hepatitis B immunoglobulin right after birth. This fact must be clarified during prenatal checkups; do not wait until after delivery to ask about it. Details on screening requirements for mothers can be found in Section 1.

title: Ensure your child receives all vaccines in the national immunization schedule at no cost; missed doses can be added later
cost_desc: Absolutely free. Laws explicitly state that vaccination centers may not charge any fees for administering vaccines on the national schedule. You’ll need to visit the clinic several times according to your child’s age. Be sure to keep the vaccination record safe and never lose it.
benefit_desc: Daycare centers and schools must verify that children have received all required vaccines on schedule. If any gaps are found, they must inform vaccination centers so guardians can be urged to complete the missing doses. Thus, missing vaccines cannot be ignored — they must be addressed before school entry. The current guidelines date to 2026. Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine is now part of the national schedule. The starting age for DTaP vaccination has been lowered from 3 months to 2 months; a total of five doses are required at 2, 4, 6 months, 18 months, and age 6. Starting March 2026, children in Tibet, Qinghai, Xinjiang, and the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps will also routinely receive Japanese encephalitis vaccine. Multiple vaccines may be administered on the same day per current protocols, provided they are injected into separate sites; mixing different vaccines into one syringe is strictly prohibited. For inactivated vaccines, oral live vaccines, and other types, no minimum interval is required between doses. For children under 18, the rule is to catch up as soon as possible — only the missing doses must be given, not the whole series from scratch. Switching manufacturers poses no problem. (National guidelines, 2026 edition)
plain_terms: All vaccines included in the national immunization schedule are completely free — clinics cannot charge a single cent. Both daycare centers and schools require proof of vaccination, so any missed doses will definitely be noticed and must be made up later. You only need to receive the remaining doses; there’s no need to restart the entire series from the beginning. Even if a different manufacturer produces the same vaccine, it can still be used. Conditions such as eczema, hives, allergic rhinitis, asthma, and even neonatal jaundice do not prevent vaccination, provided the condition remains stable.
notes: A common misconception is that children with weaker health should delay vaccination. In reality, having an “allergic constitution,” a family history of allergies, or prior food or drug allergies does not constitute a barrier to vaccination. Conditions such as atopic dermatitis (eczema), hives, allergic rhinitis, and bronchial asthma can all be managed safely provided they remain under control. Children taking antihistamines or inhaled corticosteroids may also be vaccinated. Physiological or breast milk–related neonatal jaundice poses no issue either. The only true contraindications are prior occurrence of acute severe allergic reactions to a specific vaccine or known hypersensitivity to any component of that vaccine. Children with immune deficiencies, undergoing chemotherapy or radiotherapy, or on immunosuppressive therapy require individualized assessment by a medical professional prior to vaccination. For details on the first dose of hepatitis B vaccine, refer to section 2. Non‑schedule vaccines sold at additional cost are unrelated to this free program.

title: Breastfeed exclusively for the first 6 months — no water needed; introduce solids at 6 months while continuing breastfeeding
cost_desc: This costs nothing; it even saves money compared to formula. The main “cost” is time — breastfeeding takes up a lot of daily effort. The real challenge is maintaining this routine; breastfeeding must continue without interruption during the first 6 months.
benefit_desc: The World Health Organization recommends initiating breastfeeding within the first hour after birth. It also advises exclusive breastfeeding for the first 6 months — meaning no other foods or liquids, not even water — followed by the gradual introduction of safe, adequate solid foods while continuing breastfeeding until at least age 2. The national Health Commission’s guidelines likewise promote exclusive breastfeeding from birth to 6 months, and further stipulate that solid foods given after 6 months must contain iron-rich animal products.
plain_terms: Breastfeeding should begin within the first hour after birth. For the first 6 months, infants only need breast milk — no water or other fluids are required. At 6 months, solid foods can be introduced, while breastfeeding should be continued until age 2 or beyond. These solid foods must include iron-rich animal-based products. If breast milk is insufficient or unavailable, formula is a perfectly acceptable alternative — there is no need to feel guilty. The choice between breast milk and formula has far less impact on a child’s survival than ensuring they sleep on their back.
notes: If breast milk is insufficient or not an option, formula is a perfectly acceptable substitute — there is no need for guilt. The difference between breastfeeding and formula feeding is far smaller than the impact of ensuring safe sleeping practices. As for frequency of solid food intake: infants aged 6–8 months should consume solids 1–2 times daily, while those aged 9–12 months should have 2–3 servings per day. Their daily diet must include at least four of the seven essential food groups. For infants with severe eczema or egg allergies, the question of whether to avoid peanuts is addressed in Section 12 of this chapter — the answer is: there is no need to avoid peanuts.

title: Use water hotter than 70 °C to prepare formula, then let it cool before feeding; discard any leftovers.
cost_desc: No monetary cost. It only requires a few extra minutes of waiting for the milk to cool. The difficulty lies in the fact that even when a baby is crying from hunger, caregivers must still wait for the water temperature to drop before mixing the formula.
benefit_desc: Formula milk is not sterile and may harbor Cronobacter sakazakii. Reported mortality rates among newborns infected with this bacterium fall between 40% and 80%. Experimental studies show that when hot water is first added to the bottle and the temperature is allowed to drop to roughly 73.8 °C prior to adding formula, the milk temperature stays above 70 °C in most cases. This process reduces the concentration of Cronobacter sakazakii by more than 5 logarithmic units, effectively bringing it down to under one ten-thousandth of its original amount.
plain_terms: Formula milk is not sterile and may contain a bacterium called Cronobacter sakazakii. Once newborns are infected, reported mortality rates range from 40% to 80%. To minimize this risk, first pour hot water into the feeding bottle, then wait until the temperature drops to around 73.8 °C before adding the formula. At this point, the milk remains above 70 °C, which can reduce the amount of this bacterium to less than one ten-thousandth of its original level. After preparation, let the milk cool completely before feeding, and discard any portions that are not consumed.
notes: The 70 °C threshold is specified in public health guidelines. Beary et al. explicitly state: “Public health guidelines for caregivers of high-risk infants recommend using water heated to at least 70 °C (158 °F) to prepare infant formula, in order to inactivate harmful microorganisms.” Premature infants, those with low birth weight, and babies under 2 months of age are at the highest risk of infection. Never use water that has been stored in a thermos for a full day to prepare formula, and do not leave prepared milk at room temperature for later use.

title: Do not feed honey to children under 1 year old
cost_desc: No cost involved
benefit_desc: According to the Chinese CDC, “Do not feed honey to children under 1 year of age” because “honey may contain bacteria that cause botulism.” An adult’s gut microbiome can suppress these bacterial spores — the dormant form of the bacteria — while a baby’s cannot.
plain_terms: Never give honey to babies under 1 year of age. This includes honey water, honey mixed into baby food, and any baked goods containing honey. Honey can contain bacteria that cause botulism. An adult’s gut microbiome is able to keep these bacteria in check, but a baby’s cannot. The same rule applies to homemade pickled foods and fermented products.
notes: Foods and drinks to avoid include honey water, honey mixed into baby food, and any pastries containing honey. Likewise, homemade pickled foods and fermented products should not be given to infants.

title: Vitamin K injection at birth is essential
cost_desc: 0 to several dozen yuan. This cost is usually already included in the overall hospital delivery fee, so no extra payment is required.
benefit_desc: Newborns possess minimal vitamin K reserves. Failure to supplement may result in vitamin K deficiency bleeding, with the delayed type frequently presenting as intracranial hemorrhage. Belgian medical guidelines recommend a single intramuscular injection of 1–2 mg of vitamin K at birth. In areas lacking systematic prevention programs, the incidence of vitamin K deficiency bleeding is 478 cases per 100,000 newborns, based on data from 42,000 infants in Tashkent. The authors estimate that such preventive measures can lower the incidence by more than 78.5%.
plain_terms: Newborns naturally have very little vitamin K stored in their bodies. Without supplementation, it can lead to vitamin K deficiency bleeding; the delayed form often manifests as bleeding inside the brain. In regions where this injection isn’t routinely given, the incidence of such bleeding is about 478 cases per 100,000 newborns. Administering the injection is estimated to reduce this rate by over 78%. In China, all reputable hospitals routinely provide this injection during delivery. For home births or births at unregulated facilities, parents should proactively ask whether it was given.
notes: In reputable Chinese hospitals, this injection is administered routinely, so parents need not worry about it. However, for home births or births at unlicensed facilities, it’s crucial to confirm whether the injection was given. Oral administration is less effective than intramuscular injection.

title: Infants under 3 months with a body temperature of 38°C should be taken straight to the hospital — no home observation needed
cost_desc: Registration and tests cost several hundred yuan.
benefit_desc: The American Academy of Pediatrics has issued specific guidelines for full-term infants aged 8 to 60 days who appear to be in decent health. These guidelines define fever as a body temperature of 38.0°C or higher. They further divide this age group into three subgroups — 8 to 21 days, 22 to 28 days, and 29 to 60 days — each with its own recommended course of action. Infants under 8 days old are not covered by these guidelines at all, which makes it even more imperative to seek medical care right away at this stage.
plain_terms: Infants under 3 months of age with a body temperature of 38°C must be taken to the hospital right away. Do not wait at home, and do not give them fever reducers first to see if symptoms improve. Even if an infant at this age has a serious bacterial infection, fever may be the only symptom they show. Therefore, the fact that a baby seems alert and in good spirits is not a valid reason to keep them at home. For infants under 8 days old, there are no relevant medical guidelines at all, so they must be seen by a doctor immediately.
notes: Infants at this age can have serious bacterial infections that only manifest as fever. So, the fact that a baby seems alert and in good spirits is not a valid reason to keep them at home. Do not give them fever reducers first and then wait to see if symptoms improve.

title: No matter how tired or angry you are, never shake a baby
cost_desc: There is no monetary cost. The real difficulty lies in resisting the urge to shake a baby when you’re exhausted or upset.
benefit_desc: Because a baby’s head is proportionally large and their neck muscles are underdeveloped, violent shaking can result in intracranial and retinal hemorrhage — bleeding in both the brain and eyes. This can be fatal or leave lasting impairments. Such harm is distinct from any gentle rocking used to calm them. Medically, injuries caused by shaking or impact are termed “abusive head trauma.” This condition is the leading cause of death from head injuries among children under 2 years old. In the United States between 1999 and 2014, it accounted for nearly 2,250 deaths of children under 5.
plain_terms: A baby’s head makes up a large proportion of their body size, yet their neck muscles are still very weak. Shaking them forcefully can cause bleeding inside the brain and eyes, potentially leading to death or lifelong disabilities. Gentle rocking while trying to soothe them is not dangerous; the real risk comes from uncontrolled, violent shaking. When you feel yourself losing control, place the baby back in their crib and step away for a few minutes. Letting them cry for a short while is far safer than holding them and shaking them.
notes: When you truly feel you’re about to lose control, the safest action is to return the baby to their crib and leave the room for a few minutes. Allowing them to cry briefly is much safer than holding them and shaking them. This advice is especially vital for parents who care for their children alone and often suffer from sleep deprivation. For guidance on managing your own emotions, please refer to Section 3.

title: When choosing diapers, focus on three things: fit, how often you change them, and whether they’ve been flagged in any quality inspections.
cost_desc: Prices range from a few hundred to over a thousand yuan per month, depending on the brand and quality level you choose. The absolute cost falls between 200 and 300 yuan per month.
benefit_desc: Since no official body has released any “best brand” list, this guide does not recommend any specific brands. The only verifiable data comes from two categories: first, inspection reports on product quality released by the State Administration for Market Regulation; second, official investigations into particular incidents. Following public concern in June 2026 over formaldehyde levels in infant diapers, the Administration formed a joint task force to conduct further checks.
plain_terms: No government agency has ever published an official ranking of “the best diaper brands.” The only information available comes from two sources: quality inspection reports issued by the State Administration for Market Regulation, and official investigations into specific incidents. A higher price tag does not guarantee safety, nor does being an imported product mean it meets safety standards. It’s wise to start by buying a small pack and using it for a week to check if your child develops rashes or skin irritation; only then should you consider buying in bulk.
notes: At the time of its formation, the task force stated only that “relevant findings would be released in due course.” As of September 30, 2026, neither the Administration’s official website nor recent national inspection reports contain any conclusions regarding infant diapers. In practice, higher cost does not equal greater safety, and imported products are not automatically compliant. Begin with a small trial pack to monitor for skin reactions; remember that rashes often stem from infrequent changes or poor breathability rather than brand choice. Instructions on how to access inspection reports are provided in Section 5.

title: Consider buying big-ticket items in the order “borrow, buy used, buy new” — don’t buy them all at once
cost_desc: No extra money is needed; the amount saved is usually in the thousands of yuan. The hard part is resisting the urge to buy everything at once.
benefit_desc: Strollers, cribs, blankets, and toys are all used for only a brief period, and the used market offers far more of them than there’s demand for. The only two items you really shouldn’t try to save money on — or buy used — are car seats and mattresses. Any structural damage to a car seat after a crash simply can’t be seen by looking at it.
plain_terms: Strollers, cribs, blankets, and toys are used for only a short time, and there’s plenty of them on the used market with few buyers. First, try to borrow them; if that’s not possible, buy used; only then should you consider buying new — this usually saves you thousands of yuan. However, it’s not advisable to buy used car seats or mattresses, since any structural damage from prior crashes isn’t visible to the naked eye. Things like postpartum care centers and early-education classes are optional big expenses; wait at least 24 hours before deciding.
notes: This book neither recommends nor discourages postpartum care centers, early-education classes, or baby swimming classes. Still, they’re all optional big expenses, so the 24-hour cooling-off period described in Section 5 applies to them.

title: For children with severe eczema or egg allergy, don’t avoid peanuts — introduce them early under medical guidance, but never feed whole peanuts.
cost_desc: A jar of peanut butter costs just a few dozen yuan. Feeding it a few times a week is easy to fit into a routine. Before starting, though, a doctor’s evaluation is required.
benefit_desc: The LEAP trial involved 640 infants aged 4–11 months with severe eczema, egg allergy, or both. One group ate peanut products regularly while the other avoided them entirely; at 60 months, only 1.9% of the eaters had a peanut allergy versus 13.7% of avoiders (P<0.001). Among 98 children with a weak positive skin test at entry, 10.6% of eaters were allergic versus 35.3% of avoiders (P=0.004). No serious adverse events differed between groups.
plain_terms: In a randomized trial of 640 high‑risk infants, those who ate peanuts regularly from 4 to 11 months of age had a peanut allergy rate of only 1.9% by age 5, compared with 13.7% in the group that completely avoided peanuts. Among children already showing a weak positive skin test at enrollment, the rates were 10.6% versus 35.3%. Avoiding peanuts actually raises the risk of allergy. However, whole peanuts must never be given, as they can block the airway. A total of 530 infants had negative skin tests at entry, while 98 had weakly positive results.
notes: Peanuts must be given only as thinned peanut butter or powdered form mixed into food — never as whole nuts. The Health Commission clearly states: “Whole peanuts, nuts, jelly, and similar foods can be inhaled into the airway and cause choking; infants should avoid them.” For choking first aid, see Section 13, Item 26. This guidance applies only to high‑risk children with severe eczema or egg allergy. A medical assessment is mandatory before introduction; in the LEAP trial, children with a skin‑test reaction greater than 4 mm were excluded. Another study of 1,162 breastfed infants found no significant difference in overall food allergy rates between early‑introduction and standard groups, though a subset showed a clear benefit: 5.6% versus 7.1% (P=0.32) and 2.4% versus 7.3% respectively. Evidence for typical infants is far weaker. Early introduction appears safe, but Chinese official guidelines currently give no recommendation on this point; therefore this advice follows international trial evidence. Keep in mind that LEAP started at 4 months while Chinese practice recommends waiting until 6 months for solids — consult a doctor on timing and method for high‑risk children.

title: Watch newborn jaundice for these signals: yellow within 24 hours of birth, unarousable or refusing feeds — go to hospital the same day; progressively deepening jaundice or pale stools — get evaluated promptly
cost_desc: Registration plus bilirubin testing, within a few hundred yuan. Phototherapy if needed is usually about two days in hospital. The hard part is making the trip even when the baby still looks okay.
benefit_desc: The American Academy of Pediatrics 2022 guideline states that “more than 80% of newborns will have some degree of jaundice.” High bilirubin can cause acute bilirubin encephalopathy and kernicterus. The guideline calls kernicterus “permanent crippling neurological disease,” with choreoathetoid cerebral palsy, upward gaze palsy, enamel dysplasia of primary teeth, and hearing loss. “Jaundice appearing within 24 hours after birth” is listed as a risk factor for severe hyperbilirubinemia. The UK NHS parent guidance has two tiers. Tier one: call emergency services or go to emergency — jaundice plus more sleepy than usual or hard to wake, not feeding, floppy or stiff, or seizures; jaundice before 24 hours of age also counts. Tier two: see a doctor urgently — after 24 hours, jaundice not improving or worsening, dark yellow or brown urine, or pale cream-colored stools. Globally, an estimated 480,000 newborns in 2010 had Rh hemolytic disease (ABO/Rh incompatibility) or extreme hyperbilirubinemia; 24% died and 13% developed kernicterus. Among survivors of kernicterus, more than 83% had one or more lasting impairments. Pale stools may indicate biliary atresia; Kasai procedure before 60 days of age greatly improves prognosis. Since 2004 Taiwan printed stool color cards in every newborn health handbook; surgery within 60 days rose from 60% in 2004 to 74.3% in 2005. After the cards, mortality in biliary atresia fell from 26.2% to 15.9% in a Taiwan population study — before-after, not a randomized trial.
plain_terms: More than four in five newborns have some jaundice; most clear on their own. Yellow before 24 hours of age, or unusually sleepy and unarousable, refusing feeds, floppy or stiff — go to hospital the same day. Jaundice that progressively deepens after 24 hours, or pale or white stools, also requires prompt evaluation; pale stools may indicate biliary atresia. Very high bilirubin can injure the brain and cause lifelong disability.
notes: Phototherapy uses special light on the skin to change bilirubin into forms that are easier to excrete. Do not substitute sunbathing at home: the AAP says sun exposure is hard to make both safe and effective, so it is not recommended as treatment. Do not give water or glucose water to “flush” jaundice — the guideline also advises against that. Visual yellow depth does not reliably estimate bilirubin level. UK NICE says not to rely on eyes alone; if unsure, measure once. Babies born before 38 weeks, siblings who had phototherapy, or insufficient breastfeeding raise risk of severe jaundice. Follow-up per the national basic public health service norm: home visit within one week after discharge; community health center or township clinic at 28–30 days — both visits check jaundice. If discharge orders include bilirubin recheck, go on that schedule. Full-term jaundice beyond 14 days or preterm beyond 21 days: NICE requires conjugated bilirubin testing and checking stool color. Jaundice alone does not delay vaccines (this section item 3). Newborn screening: Section 27, item 13 (heel-prick screening).

title: If pregnant or breastfeeding on a vegan diet, take vitamin B12 supplements or consume fortified foods; infant complementary foods must include animal-source foods, and consult a pediatrician before imposing a strict vegan diet
cost_desc: A bottle of vitamin B12 supplements costs only a few dollars for several months' supply (one tablet daily). Adding eggs, meat, or fish to infant complementary foods costs minimal additional money. The primary friction is overcoming cognitive inertia or family dietary beliefs if the household assumes a pure vegan diet is unconditionally healthier for infants.
benefit_desc: A Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) investigation documented severe neurologic impairment in exclusively breastfed infants of vegan mothers due to cobalamin (vitamin B12) deficiency. In one clinical case, an infant whose mother had adhered to a strict vegan diet for 7 years was hospitalized at 15 months old presenting with profound failure to thrive, severe megaloblastic anemia, and brain MRI showing severe global cerebral atrophy. Despite immediate high-dose intramuscular cyanocobalamin therapy producing hematologic recovery, cognitive and expressive speech delays persisted at 32 months of age. The CDC emphasized that maternal dietary deficiency is the leading cause of infantile cobalamin deficiency, typically emerging between 4 and 8 months of age. Because natural plant-derived B12 analogues are biologically inactive or poorly absorbed in humans, unfortified plant foods cannot provide reliable cobalamin. CDC guidance mandates that all vegan and vegetarian women who are pregnant or nursing obtain adequate daily B12 via reliable fortified foods or supplements. Similarly, the European Society for Paediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Nutrition (ESPGHAN) 2017 Committee on Nutrition position paper states that all infants require nutrient-dense, iron-rich complementary foods including meat or fortified foods, warning that vegan diets should be undertaken only under rigorous medical or dietetic supervision with parents explicitly warned of potential catastrophic developmental outcomes. Public health guidelines reinforce that daily complementary feeding must include at least four food groups, encompassing at least one animal-source food, one vegetable, and one staple grain or tuber.
plain_terms: Vitamin B12 occurs naturally almost exclusively in animal-source foods (meat, poultry, eggs, fish, and dairy). If an expectant or nursing mother eats a strict vegan diet without supplementation, her breast milk becomes profoundly deficient in B12. Breastfed infants typically manifest clinical consequences between 4 and 8 months of age: growth failure, severe developmental delay, hypotonia, and microcephaly, with prolonged deficiency causing irreversible neurological damage. Complementary infant feeding must incorporate animal-source foods daily.
notes: Controversy: The Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics (AND, 2016) states that well-planned vegetarian and vegan diets can be nutritionally adequate for all life stages, including pregnancy, lactation, infancy, and childhood. However, AND explicitly emphasizes that vegans must consume reliable sources of vitamin B12 through regular fortified foods or dietary supplements. While professional societies debate whether pure vegan feeding of infants is advisable even with supplementation, there is absolute scientific consensus across all medical bodies that maternal vegan diets require mandatory B12 supplementation. Lacto-ovo vegetarians face lower risk, but individuals consuming minimal dairy or eggs remain susceptible to subclinical depletion. Early infant B12 deficiency symptoms are non-specific (lethargy, feeding difficulties, hypotonia); CDC notes standard newborn blood counts may not detect early neurologic deficiency before structural injury occurs. If an infant displays growth stalling or motor regression, parents must proactively inform clinicians of the family's dietary pattern. Do not reject evidence-based therapies in favor of unverified alternative diets (see Chapter 16, Rule 4). Introducing complementary solids at 6 months is covered in Chapter 20, Rule 4; prenatal folic acid supplementation is covered in Chapter 27, Rule 1. Benefit magnitude is categorized as Moderate based on prevention of irreversible neurological disability. Primary beneficiaries are infants and nursing mothers.

title: Do not buy wheeled infant walkers; replace them with stationary activity centers without wheels or playpens
cost_desc: Free; in fact, saves the expense of buying a baby walker. Stationary activity centers or playpens can be bought or borrowed. The only friction is declining gifts from well-meaning relatives or throwing out an already purchased walker.
benefit_desc: U.S. National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS) data from 1990 to 2014 recorded an estimated 230,676 emergency department visits for walker-related injuries among infants younger than 15 months. Of these, 90.6% sustained injuries to the head or neck, and 74.1% resulted from falling down stairs while seated in the walker. Hospital admissions accounted for 4.5%, with skull fractures making up 37.8% of admitted cases. Following the 2010 U.S. mandatory safety standard, annual walker injuries dropped 22.7% compared to the preceding four years, yet researchers emphasized that walkers remain a persistent and entirely preventable source of severe trauma. The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) policy statement recorded 34 walker-related infant deaths in the U.S. between 1973 and 1998, noting that warning labels, public education, adult supervision, and stair gates consistently fail to prevent catastrophic accidents. Given the absence of developmental benefits, the AAP recommends a total ban on the manufacture and sale of wheeled infant walkers, recommending stationary activity centers instead. Furthermore, walkers do not accelerate motor development and may even delay it: an Irish cross-sectional study of 190 infants found walker users achieved independent walking on average 3 weeks later than non-users (61.1 weeks vs. 58.1 weeks), with greater delay correlating with heavier use. A 2002 meta-analysis found small delays in locomotor milestones ranging from 11 to 26 days across studies.
plain_terms: A baby in a wheeled walker can propel themselves more than 3 feet (0.9 meters) in a single second; in most recorded injuries, a supervising adult was in the same room. Between 1990 and 2014 in the United States, roughly 230,000 emergency department visits involved infant walkers, with 90% suffering head and neck injuries, predominantly from tumbling down stairs. Walkers do not teach infants how to walk.
notes: Canada enacted a comprehensive ban on the sale, advertising, and importation of baby walkers on April 7, 2004, extending even to secondhand sales at garage sales or flea markets under the Canada Consumer Product Safety Act. In other jurisdictions, product safety standards regulate mechanical stability and braking at drop-offs, but cannot prevent children from propelling themselves toward stairs, pulling hot liquids from tables, or falling into pools and bathtubs. Recommended safe alternatives include stationary activity centers without wheels (swivel/bounce seats), floor playpens, and high chairs. Always verify daycare or caregiver environments are free of wheeled walkers. For nursery gear purchasing sequence, see Chapter 20, Rule 11.

title: Supplement 400 IU of vitamin D daily from birth, especially for breastfed infants; full-term infants generally do not need routine calcium supplements during the first 6 months
cost_desc: Vitamin D drops cost only a few dollars per bottle (one drop daily). The main friction is remembering to administer it consistently every day until at least 1 year of age.
benefit_desc: A 2020 Cochrane systematic review confirmed that human breast milk has low vitamin D concentrations, leaving exclusively breastfed infants vulnerable to deficiency. The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) and public health authorities advise keeping infants out of direct sun exposure, necessitating oral supplementation for all infants.
