The grade B rating reflects that these figures come from adverse event reports; we have no data on how many women took these drugs without experiencing any issues. The “moderate” benefit rating reflects the seriousness of these outcomes, even though they occur infrequently.

title: Buying omeprazole over the counter for heartburn and acid reflux — use it for no more than 7 days; see a doctor immediately if you have trouble swallowing, vomit blood, or pass black stools
cost_desc: No cost involved — just follow the dosage instructions on the package.
benefit_desc: In its Announcement No. 68 of 2022, the National Medical Products Administration reclassified omeprazole enteric-coated tablets from a prescription drug to an over-the-counter medication, and released a standard package insert for it. The approved indication listed in the insert is “short-term relief of heartburn and acid reflux caused by excess stomach acid”. The precautions section specifies that the drug must not be used for more than 7 days, and that patients should consult a physician or pharmacist if symptoms persist. It also states that the drug must not be taken again within two months, and that immediate medical attention is required if symptoms recur. Use is prohibited if a patient has trouble swallowing, throat pain, vomit blood, or passes black stools, as these are possible indicators of serious illness. For patients showing warning signs such as unexplained weight loss, repeated vomiting, trouble swallowing, vomit blood, or black stools, malignant tumors must be ruled out first, since treatment with this drug may conceal symptoms and delay diagnosis. Patients over 55 years old with new or changing symptoms should consult a doctor before use. People taking clopidogrel must avoid taking omeprazole at the same time.
plain_terms: Since 2022, omeprazole enteric-coated tablets have been available over the counter without a prescription. However, the package instructions clearly state that you should only take it for up to 7 days, and avoid using it again within two months. If you experience trouble swallowing, pain in the throat, vomit blood, or pass black stools, do not take it on your own — these are potential signs of serious medical conditions. This medication can also mask symptoms of stomach cancer, potentially delaying an accurate diagnosis.
notes: Clopidogrel is a blood-thinning medication commonly prescribed to patients who have had a stent implanted or a myocardial infarction. Omeprazole can reduce its effectiveness, so patients taking clopidogrel must consult a doctor first. The evidence grade is set to B because these requirements are stipulated in the official package insert, and no research has been conducted to quantify how many adverse events can be prevented by following these instructions. The benefit level is rated “moderate” because while this medication helps prevent delayed diagnosis of stomach bleeding or stomach cancer, most cases of heartburn and acid reflux are not severe.

title: Don’t ask doctors for antibiotics for the common cold
cost_desc: It costs nothing and can even save you money on medicine.
benefit_desc: A Cochrane systematic review pooled data from 6 randomized trials involving 1,147 participants. When comparing antibiotic use to placebo for treating colds, there was no significant difference in the proportion of people who did not recover or whose symptoms persisted (RR 0.83, 95% CI 0.60–1.14, no statistically significant difference). The risk of adverse reactions was 1.8 times higher than in the placebo group (95% CI 1.01–3.21). For adults specifically, this risk was 2.62 times higher (1.32–5.18), while no increase was observed in children (RR 0.91, 0.51–1.63). For acute purulent rhinitis where nasal discharge with pus lasts less than 10 days, antibiotics also showed no clear benefit (RR 0.73, 0.47–1.13). However, the risk of adverse reactions rose by roughly 46% (RR 1.46, 1.10–1.94). The authors concluded that routine use of antibiotics is not recommended for either of these conditions.
plain_terms: Taking antibiotics for a cold doesn’t speed up recovery compared to not taking them at all. For adults, the risk of side effects is more than twice as high when using antibiotics. For cases where nasal discharge with pus lasts less than 10 days, there is no clear benefit to taking antibiotics either.
notes: This updated version was released in 2025; the abstract states that literature searches were conducted up to 2013. Antibiotics are prescription-only drugs in China, so pharmacies must sell them only with a valid prescription. Do not take leftover antibiotics at home without medical advice. The “moderate” rating for benefits is based on the fact that antibiotics primarily reduce the risk of adverse reactions rather than preventing death.

title: For diarrhea, start by drinking oral rehydration solution; do not give anti-diarrheal drugs to children under 5
cost_desc: A box of oral rehydration solution costs just a few dollars, so it’s worth keeping one at home.
benefit_desc: WHO’s guidelines on diarrhea treatment state clearly that anti-diarrheal and anti-vomiting drugs provide no real benefit for children with acute or prolonged diarrhea. They do not prevent dehydration or improve nutritional status, and some carry serious, even fatal side effects — so they must never be given to children under 5. Drugs like loperamide that slow intestinal motility can lead to severe paralytic intestinal obstruction, which is potentially fatal and can prolong the underlying infection. The same guidelines also warn that drinks high in sugar draw water into the intestines, causing hypernatremic dehydration; this applies to soft drinks and most commercially sold fruit juices. WHO recommends a low-osmolarity formula with a total osmotic pressure of 245 mOsm/L; compared to older formulations, this reduces unplanned intravenous fluid administration by 33%. A Cochrane review of 8 trials reached similar conclusions (OR 0.59, 95% CI 0.45–0.79), showing roughly a 40% reduction in complications when this solution is used.
plain_terms: The most important thing during diarrhea is rehydration, not stopping the diarrhea itself. Mix the solution exactly as directed on the package and drink it — never substitute it with sugary juices or soft drinks, as the excess sugar can actually worsen dehydration. Never give anti-diarrheal medications such as loperamide to kids under 5 years old; in severe cases these drugs can cause life-threatening intestinal blockages.
notes: When purchasing oral rehydration solution, always check the package label for its osmotic pressure and choose the low-osmolarity version. The WHO guidelines also note that blood in a child’s stool almost always indicates bacterial dysentery, which requires medical treatment with antibiotics — rehydration alone is not sufficient. The “moderate” benefit rating here reflects the fact that the available data compares two different rehydration solutions rather than the effect of drinking any solution versus none.

title: Don’t take painkillers for more than 15 days a month; limit combination painkillers to 10 days. Otherwise, headaches may actually be caused by the medication itself.
cost_desc: No direct cost. You’ll just need to keep track of how many days you’ve taken the medicine, and resist the urge to pop pills at every sign of a headache.
benefit_desc: The third edition of the International Classification of Headache published by the International Headache Society outlines the diagnostic criteria for this condition. It applies to people who already have a history of headaches, experience headaches on 15 or more days each month, and have been regularly taking excessive amounts of headache medication for over 3 months. For standard non-opioid painkillers, the threshold for overuse is 15 days per month; for combination painkillers, it is 10 days per month. This classification is backed by robust epidemiological evidence, and most patients see positive results after reducing their medication intake.
plain_terms: If you take painkillers frequently for recurrent headaches, the medication itself may eventually provoke more frequent headaches — a clinical condition known as medication-overuse headache. The clinical threshold is taking standard single-ingredient analgesics (such as acetaminophen, ibuprofen, or aspirin) for 15 or more days per month for at least three consecutive months. For combination analgesics containing multiple active ingredients or caffeine, the threshold drops to 10 or more days per month. Rotating between different painkillers does not reset this counter. Most patients experience substantial symptom relief after systematically tapering excess pain medication under medical guidance.
notes: Painkillers with “caffeine” in their name typically contain added caffeine, so they count toward the 10-day limit for combination painkillers. If you find that your headache days are increasing month on month, it’s best to consult a neurologist rather than simply taking more medication. This evidence grade is assigned because the classification criteria serve as a diagnostic benchmark rather than being derived from controlled clinical trials. The benefit level is rated “moderate” as it primarily reduces the frequency of headaches without preventing life-threatening outcomes.

title: Clear out expired and unused medicines regularly; dispose of them with packaging in hazardous-waste bins, not at home
cost_desc: No cost. Sort the medicine cabinet once a year — about ten minutes.
benefit_desc: U.S. emergency-department surveillance estimated that from 2004 to 2013, children under 6 took medicines without adult supervision about 640,000 times (estimate 640,161 ED visits). In 2013 alone about 59,000 visits (59,092). From 2010 to 2013 the most common form was oral prescription tablets, 45.9% of cases. Among prescriptions, opioids (13.8%) and benzodiazepines (12.7%) were most common. In 2017 five U.S. poison centers surveyed callers: for prescription ingestions, 30.7% involved grandparents’ medicines. More than half (51.5%) of prescription drugs had been removed from original packaging before the child accessed them. China’s National Catalogue of Hazardous Wastes (2025 edition) classifies household discarded medicines and their packaging as hazardous waste in domestic refuse. Shanghai’s sorting guide puts waste medicines in hazardous waste, including expired drugs, capsules, tablets, and inner packaging — “discard medicines preferably with packaging.” Shanghai also requires pharmacies collecting household expired medicines to use temporary transfer points set by district market-supervision departments. The U.S. FDA states the best disposal for expired and unwanted medicines is take-back programs.
plain_terms: Nearly half of unsupervised pediatric medication ingestions involve prescription tablets. About three in ten of those prescriptions belong to grandparents. Removing unused drugs removes one thing a child can find. Put discarded medicines in hazardous-waste bins with original packaging, or hand them to pharmacies that collect old drugs.
notes: Local waste-sorting rules differ; follow the directory posted at your building’s waste room. In Shanghai, traditional Chinese medicine dregs go in wet waste, not hazardous. Keep remaining drugs in original boxes, not pill organizers or other bottles, out of children’s reach — see Section 13, item 20 (accidental ingestion). Do not self-treat with leftover antibiotics — item 7 in this section. When no U.S. take-back exists, FDA allows mixing with coffee grounds or cat litter before sealing in trash; a few strong painkillers may be flushed — that is U.S. practice; in China follow local sorting. Rated B because U.S. figures are registry counts without studies on how much cabinet cleanouts reduce ingestions. Benefit rated small: numbers are ED visits, not deaths, and the effect of cleaning cannot be calculated from them.

title: While taking cephalosporins, metronidazole, and similar antibacterials, and for 7 days after stopping, avoid alcohol — including alcohol in Huoxiang Zhengqi oral liquid and cough syrups
cost_desc: No money. Abstain from alcohol for a little over a week; check other medicines for ethanol on the label.
benefit_desc: This is a disulfiram-like reaction. A 2023 medication-safety popularization from the Fujian Provincial Medical Products Administration states that drinking before or after some cephalosporins may trigger this reaction, “which can seriously harm health or be life-threatening.” Symptoms include facial flushing, sweating, palpitations, even dyspnea, hypotension, and anaphylactic shock. Citing the Chinese Pharmacopoeia Clinical Medication Information, listed drugs include cefazolin, ceftriaxone, cefoperazone, metronidazole, tinidazole, furazolidone, and others. The article states “no alcohol or alcohol-containing drugs or foods for 7 days after dosing,” examples including liqueur chocolates and Huoxiang Zhengqi oral liquid, because the inhibited enzyme often needs 4 to 5 days to recover. One Guangzhou hospital summarized 82 cases over 2 years: cephalosporins caused 57 cases (69.51%), nitroimidazoles (metronidazole, tinidazole) 10 cases (12.20%). Alcohol from beverages 40 cases (48.78%), from ethanol-containing medicines 31 cases (37.80%) — including Huoxiang Zhengqi oral liquid, cough syrup, and motherwort extract. Of 82 cases, 68 mild, 9 moderate, 5 severe; relief within 1–3 hours; no deaths. U.S. metronidazole labeling requires no alcohol during treatment and for at least 3 days after, and no products containing propylene glycol.
plain_terms: Some cephalosporins and metronidazole can trigger flushing, palpitations, chest tightness, and vomiting when mixed with alcohol; severe cases drop blood pressure. Beer and spirits are not the only triggers — Huoxiang Zhengqi oral liquid and cough syrups with alcohol count. Avoid alcohol from the start of the drug through 7 days after the last dose.
notes: Not every cephalosporin reacts, but laypeople cannot tell them apart — follow this rule for any cephalosporin or metronidazole course. Tell the doctor if you drank recently when these are prescribed. The popularization also suggests avoiding alcohol for 3 days before dosing while noting no authoritative interval. If flushing or palpitations start, stop all alcohol immediately; mild cases may resolve on their own, severe cases need hospital care. Do not drink alcohol while taking acetaminophen — item 1 in this section. Rated B because evidence is case series and labeling, not controlled trials. Benefit rated small: all 82 cases recovered within hours, no deaths, only 5 severe.

title: Do not drive, work at heights, or operate machinery while taking cold or allergy medications containing chlorpheniramine or diphenhydramine
cost_desc: Free. Check active ingredients before taking over-the-counter multi-symptom cold or allergy formulas. Switch to public transit, taxis, or ask a clinician or pharmacist for non-sedating alternatives during treatment.
benefit_desc: National drug safety bulletins issued by the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) highlight that multi-ingredient formulas containing chlorpheniramine maleate (Piriton) cause drowsiness, fatigue, lethargy, and dry mouth. Bulletins instruct healthcare providers and retail pharmacies to warn patients: "Do not operate airplanes, automobiles, or watercraft, and do not engage in high-altitude work, machinery operation, or precision instrument manipulation during medication courses." In a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled crossover trial conducted on the Iowa driving simulator involving 40 drivers with allergic rhinitis, participants completed driving evaluations under four separate treatments: diphenhydramine 50 mg, fexofenadine 60 mg (a second-generation non-sedating antihistamine), alcohol (to blood alcohol concentration 0.10%), and placebo. Diphenhydramine produced the worst speed tracking and vehicle control performance, significantly inferior to alcohol and fexofenadine. During sudden highway incursions, drivers taking alcohol or diphenhydramine had impaired response times, while fexofenadine performance was virtually indistinguishable from placebo. Crucially, drivers' subjective drowsiness self-ratings failed to predict simulator driving impairments.
plain_terms: Many multi-ingredient cold medicines contain first-generation antihistamines like chlorpheniramine or diphenhydramine, which cause pronounced drowsiness and psychomotor slowing. Regulatory agencies strictly warn against driving, working at heights, or operating machinery while taking them. In driving simulator trials, individuals taking diphenhydramine drove worse than drivers with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.1%. Subjective feeling of alertness does not correlate with actual driving performance.
notes: Popular multi-symptom cold medications frequently combine chlorpheniramine with acetaminophen; always examine active ingredient tables. If you must drive or operate equipment, request non-drowsy second-generation antihistamines (such as fexofenadine, loratadine, or cetirizine) from your doctor or pharmacist. Many multi-symptom remedies also contain acetaminophen; see Chapter 34, Rule 1 on acetaminophen dose caps. For driving fatigue risks, see Chapter 1, Rule 9.
